Name: model_shaped_instruction_task_shaped_store
Title: Model-Shaped Instructions, Task-Shaped Stores: The Memory-Instruction Substitution Measured on One Backbone Does Not Survive a Backbone Swap
Short Hypothesis: A GEPA-optimized instruction and a retrievable experience store built from the same training episodes are not equally portable: the instruction encodes corrections to the optimizing backbone's own failure modes (model-shaped) while the store encodes task facts (task-shaped), so when both are moved unchanged to a different backbone the instruction's marginal gain collapses more than the store's, and the negative instruction-by-store interaction (substitution) measured on the source backbone shrinks toward zero or reverses on the target. The substitution ratio is therefore a property of the (backbone, optimizer) pair, not of the episode set.
Related Work: Compiled Memory / Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) compiles experience into instruction sub-bullets and asserts the compiled knowledge is task-shaped rather than model-shaped, but never tests a backbone swap against a retrieval store or an optimizer-evolved instruction built from the same episodes. PromptBridge (arXiv:2512.01420) transfers prompts across LLMs without re-optimization but has no memory arm; MulVul (arXiv:2601.18847) evolves prompts across models for vulnerability detection. MemCollab (arXiv:2603.23234) and the hierarchical teacher-memory paper (arXiv:2608.07169) transfer memory from a large to a small backbone but have no optimized-instruction arm. MemoHarness (arXiv:2607.14159) reports selective transfer of an evolved harness to unseen base models without separating instruction from memory. ExpeL's ALFWorld table has the joint cell on one backbone; MAGE (arXiv:2607.11944) runs two backbones without transfer; arXiv:2510.23730 and arXiv:2605.30785 show that the best memory design depends on backbone capability; arXiv:2604.27003 frames retrieval competition as continual learning. The brief's Q1 names the interaction sign across backbones as the unfixed part of the substitution question. Archived ideas memory_or_instruction, substitutes_not_complements and optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold all measure substitution on a single backbone; clause_level_portability studies domain transfer of prompt clauses without a memory channel.
Abstract: Coupled memory-and-prompt-optimization systems report one number on one backbone, and the archived substitution proposals in this program ask how much of a retrieval store's value survives an instruction optimized on the same episodes, again on one backbone. We claim that this residual is not a property of the episodes but of the backbone whose failures the optimizer corrected. From one pool of ALFWorld training episodes rolled out by backbone A we materialize three artifacts: a GEPA-optimized instruction I_A, an ExpeL/ReMe-style store S_A (raw and distilled items), and their combination. We evaluate the 2x2 (instruction on/off x store on/off) at length-matched prompts on A and on two unrelated backbones B (120B MoE) and C (8B), and symmetrically materialize from B's episodes. The estimands are each channel's marginal gain, the interaction term, and each channel's transfer loss. Prediction: the instruction loses more than the store under transfer and the substitution (negative interaction) measured on A shrinks or reverses on B and C; a clause-level annotation ties the lost value to clauses addressing failure categories over-represented in A. If both channels transfer equally, Atlas's task-shaped claim extends to optimizer-evolved instructions and the single-backbone residual is a stable quantity, which refutes us. Either outcome tells practitioners which artifact to keep when the backbone changes and reprices re-optimization against carrying a store.
Experiments: (1) Data: the local ALFWorld pool of 1,465 tasks split once into 300 training tasks (episode generation), 100 dev tasks (GEPA validation) and 400 held-out evaluation tasks stratified over the six task types; the same split for every arm. (2) Backbones served locally with vLLM on the 4xA100 node: A = 27B dense (Gemma-3-27B-it or Qwen3-32B), B = 120B MoE (gpt-oss-120b class), C = 8B dense (Qwen3-8B); GEPA's reflector is fixed to the source actor (A for source-A artifacts, B for source-B) so 'model-shaped' refers to the actor-plus-reflector pair, with a reflector-swap ablation to separate the two. (3) Materialization from E_A (three rollouts per training task under the seed ReAct instruction at temperature 0.7): I_A = GEPA over the system instruction with a 600-rollout budget on the dev set, three optimizer seeds; S_A = store of (a) raw successful trajectories, (b) ExpeL-style distilled insights, (c) failure notes, indexed by task type plus a single shared embedder, retrieved at k in {1,3}; combined = I_A + S_A. Repeat from E_B to obtain I_B, S_B. (4) Evaluation matrix: target T in {A,B,C} x source sigma in {A,B} x 2x2 cells x k in {1,3} x store representation {raw, insight}; off cells padded with a length-matched neutral filler so all cells in a (T, sigma) block are within 5 percent tokens; 400 tasks x 2 evaluation seeds per cell. Ceiling arms: I_T (re-optimized on the target) and S_T with their materialization cost. (5) Estimands per (T, sigma): Delta_I = success(I on, S off) minus success(none); Delta_S likewise; interaction omega = both minus I minus S plus none; transfer loss L_I(sigma to T) = Delta_I(sigma, sigma) minus Delta_I(T, sigma), L_S likewise; primary contrast D = L_I minus L_S on A to B, A to C and B to A. (6) Clause-level analysis: parse I_A into clauses; compute each backbone's baseline failure-category distribution under a 12-category ALFWorld failure taxonomy (wrong receptacle, invalid action syntax, loop, premature done, missed object, etc.) from the seed-instruction runs; label a clause model-shaped if the frequency ratio of its target category between A and B exceeds 2, else task-shaped; ablate model-shaped clauses on A and B. (7) Cost axis: episodes and tokens for materializing I_sigma and S_sigma, re-optimization cost of I_T, and injected tokens per episode, giving cost per point for carry-the-instruction, carry-the-store and re-optimize. (8) Secondary environment: WebShop with 200 held-out tasks for A to B only if budget allows.
Baselines and Ablations: Seed ReAct instruction and the published hand-written ALFWorld ReAct prompt on every backbone (non-optimized instruction transfer control); length-matched filler versus no filler (checks the padding itself is neutral); reflector swap (actor A, reflector B); store built from B's episodes evaluated on A (reverse direction, separates shape from a capability-gap explanation); raw versus distilled store items; k = 1 versus 3; re-optimized ceiling I_T with its cost; instruction-in-store control (I_A's clauses inserted as retrievable items) to test whether the store channel can carry the instruction's content; same-family pair (Qwen3-32B to Qwen3-8B) versus cross-family pair to separate family from capability.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: D = L_I minus L_S is at least 4 success-rate points for A to B and A to C with a task-cluster bootstrap 95 percent CI excluding zero; refuted if the CI includes zero or D is negative. P2: omega(A,A) is negative (substitution on the source) and omega(B,A) minus omega(A,A) is at least 3 points; refuted if the interaction is equally negative on the target. P3: removing model-shaped clauses from I_A costs at least 3 points on A and at most 1 point on B; refuted if the loss is symmetric. P4: L_S(raw) exceeds L_S(insight), since raw trajectories carry A's action style. P5: the reverse direction B to A shows the same sign of D; refuted if D flips sign with direction, which would indicate a capability-gap artifact. Null that kills the idea: D within plus or minus 2 points in both directions, meaning optimizer-evolved instructions are as task-shaped as stores.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design: every cell runs on the same 400 tasks with identical environment seeds; per-task binary outcomes; pairwise cells compared by exact McNemar; contrasts of differences (transfer losses, interaction terms, D) by cluster bootstrap over tasks with 10,000 resamples; three GEPA seeds reported individually with no best-of-seed selection; two evaluation seeds per cell give the within-cell noise floor and one full null replicate (identical cell run twice) is executed before any confirmatory run; the minimum detectable effect is pre-registered from the pilot discordance rate (expected 3 to 4 points at 80 percent power with 400 tasks x 2 seeds) and all thresholds above are fixed before confirmatory runs; per-episode token accounting for every cell; failure-category annotation by a local LLM judge calibrated on a 200-episode human-checked set with agreement reported.

Name: coupling_variance_components
Title: Whose Variance Is It? A Seed-Crossed Decomposition and Cost-Matched Audit of Memory-Coupled Prompt Optimization on Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
Short Hypothesis: On long-horizon agent tasks, the variance amplification attributed to coupling an experience memory to a reflective prompt optimizer (MAGE's Prompt Optimization Coupling Effect) is carried by the optimizer-by-bank interaction component - the evolved instruction is fit to the particular bank realization it was scored against - rather than by additive optimizer and bank main effects or by evaluation noise; and once total episode budget is matched, the coupled system's mean advantage over the better single channel lies inside the interval implied by its own variance.
Related Work: MAGE (arXiv:2607.11944) reports the coupling effect on GSM8K-Hard with two backbones and single-seed peak reporting, no variance decomposition, no agent task and no cost matching. p1 (arXiv:2604.08801) separates response stochasticity from system-prompt quality variance in order to filter training prompts; it is single-turn and memory-free. 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip' (arXiv:2604.14585) predicts when prompt optimization helps compound systems, without memory. 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' (arXiv:2602.07150) shows single-run agentic estimates are noisy and supplies only the evaluation-noise component. 'Do Agent Optimizers Compound?' (arXiv:2607.14004) compares GEPA and Meta Harness on Terminal-Bench 2.0 under continual learning, not variance components. MEMO (arXiv:2603.09022) claims coupling reduces variance in games without cost matching; the mistake-notebook optimizer (arXiv:2508.18749) admits a 3 to 5x compute increase without a cost-normalized baseline; MemAPO (arXiv:2603.21520) reports cost reduction without seeds. The program's own pilot found a null replicate matching the best treatment. Archived ideas memory_dropout_coadaptation and coadaptation_transplant_ccr diagnose co-adaptation by swapping whole artifacts and propose fixes; memory_volume_amplifies_optimizer_curse studies selection bias as a function of injection volume.
Abstract: MAGE names a Prompt Optimization Coupling Effect: adding an episodic memory and other stochastic components to a reflective prompt optimizer raises mean accuracy while amplifying variance. The finding rests on single-turn math, two backbones and peak reporting, and it says nothing about where the variance comes from or whether the mean survives cost matching. We treat the coupled system as a crossed random-effects experiment: three optimizer seeds by three independently built experience banks by two evaluation seeds, each evolved instruction evaluated against every bank, on 300 held-out ALFWorld tasks with a local 27B model as actor and reflector. A mixed model attributes variance to optimizer, bank, their interaction and evaluation noise, and a full episode-and-token ledger lets us compare the coupled system with instruction-only GEPA and store-only memory at equal total budget. We predict that the interaction component dominates (instructions are fit to the bank they were scored against, visible as an in-bank minus cross-bank gap), that the amplification replicates on an agent task, and that the cost-matched mean advantage does not clear the system's own interval. The output includes a seed-count design rule for coupled-optimizer papers. If variance is additive or dominated by evaluation noise, or if the coupled system beats both cost-matched channels, the hypothesis fails and MAGE's effect stands as a genuine mean gain on agent tasks.
Experiments: (1) System: GEPA over the ALFWorld ReAct system instruction with an ExpeL/ReMe-style store in the loop; at every optimization rollout and at test time k = 3 items are retrieved by task type plus embedding. Actor and reflector: one 27B dense local model; replication of the main claim on an 8B model and a reduced run on the 120B MoE. (2) Crossed random-effects design: optimizer seeds o in {1,2,3} x bank seeds b in {1,2,3} x evaluation seeds e in {1,2}. A bank seed is a store built from an independent re-rollout of the 300-task training pool (different sampling seed, same write policy); a stronger variant uses disjoint 150-task sub-pools per bank seed. Each (o,b) yields an instruction I_ob; every I_ob is evaluated with every bank b' (in-bank when b' = b, cross-bank otherwise) on the same 300 held-out tasks: 9 instructions x 3 banks x 2 evaluation seeds x 300 tasks = 16,200 episodes, plus controls. (3) Single-channel controls: GEPA-only (store off, 3 optimizer seeds x 2 evaluation seeds); store-only with the seed instruction (3 bank seeds x 2 evaluation seeds); none. (4) Variance decomposition: per-cell success rates modeled by a linear mixed model with random effects for optimizer seed, bank seed, their interaction and residual (evaluation seed); a task-level logistic GLMM as robustness check; components with parametric-bootstrap CIs; compare total coupled variance with sigma2_O from GEPA-only and sigma2_B from store-only. (5) Co-adaptation signature: in-bank minus cross-bank success for each I_ob. (6) Cost matching: full accounting of environment episodes and generated tokens for every arm (optimization rollouts, reflection calls, bank construction and validation, test-time injection); cost-matched arms are GEPA-only given the coupled system's total budget (more iterations and larger minibatches) and store-only given the same budget (larger bank, more validation). (7) Design-rule output: from the fitted components, the number of (optimizer, bank) seed pairs needed for a coupled system's reported gain to clear its own 95 percent interval, tabulated for effect sizes of 2, 5 and 10 points. (8) Ablations: bank-ensemble scoring during GEPA (each candidate scored under all three banks) to test whether the interaction component is reducible; frozen bank versus growing bank during optimization.
Baselines and Ablations: GEPA-only, store-only and none; hand-written expert instruction with the store; cost-matched GEPA-only and store-only; bank-ensemble scoring; frozen versus growing bank during optimization; k = 1 versus 3; overlapping versus disjoint bank sub-pools; 8B backbone replicate of the full crossed design; reflector swapped to the 120B MoE to check whether a stronger reflector removes the interaction variance.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: sigma2_OB is at least sigma2_O plus sigma2_B in the coupled system; refuted if sigma2_OB is below half of that sum with bootstrap CI. P2: variance across (o,b) cells is at least twice the GEPA-only variance across o (agent-task replication of the coupling effect); refuted if the ratio is at most 1.2. P3: in-bank minus cross-bank success is at least 3 points averaged over I_ob; refuted if at most 1 point. P4: at matched total episode budget, coupled mean minus the better of GEPA-only and store-only has a 95 percent CI containing zero; refuted if the coupled system beats both cost-matched channels by at least 4 points with CI excluding zero. P5: bank-ensemble scoring reduces sigma2_OB by at least 50 percent at a mean cost of at most 2 points. If P2 fails outright, the paper's contribution becomes the null: the coupling effect does not transfer from single-turn math to agent tasks at this scale, reported with the decomposition.
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells on the same 300 held-out tasks with identical environment seeds; evaluation seeds provide the pure noise floor and a full null replicate (the same (o,b,e) cell run twice) is executed before any confirmatory run; per-seed results reported individually with no peak selection; mean contrasts by cluster bootstrap over tasks; variance components with parametric-bootstrap CIs and a likelihood-ratio test for the interaction term; thresholds pre-registered; the minimum detectable mean difference at 300 tasks x 2 seeds is computed from the pilot discordance rate and expected around 4 points; every arm's cost is recorded in episodes and tokens so that the cost-matched comparison is exact rather than nominal.

(2) s2cli, query 'MAGE prompt optimization coupling effect episodic memory GEPA stability variance': MAGE arXiv:2607.11944 verified (multiple stochastic signals in a closed reflective loop improve performance and amplify variance, not predictable from components in isolation); 'Do Agent Optimizers Compound?' arXiv:2607.14004 (GEPA versus RELAI-VCL on Terminal-Bench 2.0, regression control); 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip' arXiv:2604.14585; p1 arXiv:2604.08801 (response stochasticity versus system-prompt quality variance, filters training prompts, outperforms GEPA, single-turn, no memory). (3) s2cli --recent, query 'memory-augmented prompt optimizer cost-normalized comparison seed variance ALFWorld': ElasticMem arXiv:2605.30690, StepOPSD arXiv:2605.27140 (RL on ALFWorld), plus the same prompt-optimization papers; no cost-matched coupled-optimizer study. (4) s2cli --recent, query 'variance components random effects seeds prompt optimization LLM agent stability evaluation noise': 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' arXiv:2602.07150 (single-run agentic estimates are noisy; multiple runs needed), 'Hallucinations Live in Variance' arXiv:2601.07058, NoisyAgent arXiv:2605.27209; no crossed-seed decomposition of an optimizer-plus-memory system. Risk Factors and Limitations: A 3 x 3 seed crossing gives wide component CIs (reported as such; extended to 4 x 4 on the 8B model if budget allows); bank seeds from re-rollouts of one pool may converge to near-identical banks (mitigated by the disjoint sub-pool variant, which however confounds bank content with pool coverage); GEPA with a local 27B reflector may be too weak on ALFWorld for the coupled system to beat the seed prompt at all, in which case the study documents that; the linear mixed model on cell means assumes near-Gaussian cell rates, checked with the GLMM; results are specific to GEPA plus an ExpeL/ReMe store on ALFWorld; the 120B replicate is under-powered; total budget about 20,000 episodes for the main design plus about 8,000 for controls and cost-matched arms, roughly three to five days on 4xA100.
Addresses gap: G4 (seed variance and cost normalization of memory-coupled optimizers relative to simpler baselines) as primary; G2 as secondary, because the decomposition is run on a long-horizon agent task rather than single-turn math.
Not a restatement of: Nearest prior-result bullet: 'Noise swallowed most claims ... a null replicate with no treatment produced the same apparent gain as the best real treatment' - that measured evaluation noise for a single optimizer; this idea decomposes a coupled system's variance into optimizer, bank, interaction and evaluation components and matches cost. Nearest digest card: arxiv:2607.11944 (MAGE: coupling raises mean while amplifying variance on GSM8K-Hard) - this idea claims which component carries the amplification, tests it on agent tasks, and asks whether the mean survives cost matching. Nearest archived idea: memory_dropout_coadaptation (bank-swap diagnostic and which fix survives turnover) - this idea makes no fix its claim; it quantifies variance components and the cost-matched mean and derives a seed-count design rule.

Name: optimizer_writes_the_read_policy
Title: The Optimizer Writes the Read Policy: Joint Instruction-Memory Optimization Gains Are Carried by Evolved Clauses That Govern Memory Use, Not by Better Task Instructions
Short Hypothesis: When a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is run with the experience store in the loop, its reflections attribute failures to misapplied retrieved items and evolve read-policy clauses (when to trust, verify, or ignore retrieved experience); these clauses, not task clauses, carry the joint system's advantage over the sum of the two channels, they matter only in the high-k regime where injected experience harms, and they match explicit read-time controls (utility filtering, similarity abstention) at zero runtime cost.
Related Work: Controllable Memory Usage (arXiv:2601.05107) models memory reliance as a user-set dial in conversational settings; the Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows harm begins at the first adopted conflicting item and evaluates no control; MemTrapBench (arXiv:2608.20202) proposes a hand-designed inference-time strategy against memory-induced reasoning traps; MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192) filters items by learned utility; Live-Evo (arXiv:2602.02369) keeps an experience bank and a meta-guideline bank online but does not test whether guidelines govern experience use; REVERE (arXiv:2603.20667), Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666), MEMO (arXiv:2603.09022) and MAGE (arXiv:2607.11944) couple memory and prompt evolution without inspecting what the evolved prompt says about the memory; GEPA (arXiv:2507.19457) is described as learning high-level rules from trial and error; 'Honest Lying' (arXiv:2605.29463) shows reflexive agents store confident wrong interpretations; contextual drag (arXiv:2602.04288) shows failed attempts in context bias later generations. Archived ideas substitutes_not_complements (content substitution at clause level), instruction_conditioned_complementarity (content overlap decides help or harm), memory_vetoes_instruction_slot (memory suppresses instruction compliance), commit_then_consult_slot_discipline (commitment order) and coadaptation_transplant_ccr (whole-artifact transplants) do not identify an optimizer-discovered read policy as the mediator.
Abstract: Systems that evolve a prompt while an experience store sits in the loop report a joint gain but never read what the evolved prompt says about the store. We propose that a reflective optimizer, seeing traces in which retrieved items were misapplied, writes read-policy clauses (verify a retrieved plan against the current observation, ignore examples from other task types, prefer the environment over memory when they disagree) and that these clauses, not improved task clauses, are the mechanism of the joint gain. On ALFWorld with a local 27B model we run GEPA with the store off (I_solo) and on (I_joint) at two injection sizes, annotate every clause as read-policy, task or format, and test mediation by removing the read-policy clauses from I_joint, transplanting them onto I_solo, and, as the competing mediator, removing task clauses whose content overlaps the store. We compare the evolved read policy head-to-head with utility filtering, similarity abstention and provenance gating at the injection size where memory harms, counting the clean-setting cost. Predictions: the clause share and the mediated fraction are large only in the high-k regime, transplant recovers most of the joint gain, and the evolved clauses match explicit controls at zero runtime cost. If the optimizer writes no such clauses, or removing them leaves the joint gain intact, the interaction must be explained by content substitution and the archived account stands.
Experiments: (1) Setting: ALFWorld with a 27B dense local backbone as actor and reflector; 300 training tasks for store construction and GEPA rollouts, 100 dev tasks, 300 held-out tasks. Store: ExpeL-style insights plus raw trajectories, retrieved by task type plus embedding at k in {1, 3, 7}; the harm regime is pre-screened per backbone by a k-sweep under the seed instruction and the largest-harm k is fixed as k_high before any optimization. (2) Optimizer arms: I_solo (GEPA with store off) and I_joint(k) (GEPA with store on at k) for k in {1, k_high}; three optimizer seeds each, identical rollout budget. (3) Full 2x2 per k: {I_solo, I_joint(k)} x {store off, store on at k}, plus the seed instruction, with length-matched filler in store-off cells and after clause removal so every comparison is at matched prompt length. (4) Clause annotation: split each instruction into clauses by sentence or bullet; label each as read-policy (refers to retrieved or past experience or examples and how to use them), task (ALFWorld procedure) or format/other; labels by a local LLM classifier with a full human check (instructions are 20 to 40 clauses); agreement reported; labels frozen before evaluation. (5) Mediation tests: (a) I_joint minus its read-policy clauses; (b) I_solo plus I_joint's read-policy clauses transplanted at the same relative position; (c) I_solo plus one generic hand-written read-policy sentence; (d) I_joint minus task clauses whose content overlaps store items (the content-substitution mediator); all evaluated store on and store off at k_high and k = 1. (6) Reflection-trace audit: fraction of GEPA reflections in the joint run that mention retrieved items, and the iteration at which the first read-policy clause appears, correlated with the candidate's validation gain. (7) Head-to-head against explicit read-time controls at k_high with I_solo: utility filtering (MemRL-style utility tags from training outcomes), similarity abstention (retrieve only above a swept threshold), provenance gating (success-only items); report success, the clean-setting cost (store off) and runtime cost per episode. (8) Backbone check: arms (2) to (5) replicated on an 8B model; reflector swapped to the 120B MoE in one ablation.
Baselines and Ablations: Seed instruction with and without store; I_solo with and without store; I_joint with and without store; clause-removal and clause-transplant arms; generic hand-written read-policy clause; content-overlap task-clause removal (competing mediator); explicit read-time controls (utility filtering, similarity abstention, provenance gating); k = 1 versus k_high; raw versus insight store items; reflector swap to the 120B MoE to test whether a stronger reflector writes more or fewer read-policy clauses; random-clause removal of equal length as a control for clause-removal damage.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: at least 20 percent of I_joint(k_high) clauses are read-policy clauses versus at most 5 percent in I_solo; refuted if the optimizer writes none. P2: removing read-policy clauses from I_joint(k_high) removes at least 70 percent of the joint advantage over I_solo plus store, and transplanting them onto I_solo recovers at least 70 percent; refuted if either share is below 30 percent with bootstrap CI. P3: the joint advantage and the read-policy clause share are both near zero at k = 1 and largest at k_high. P4: at k_high, read-policy clauses recover at least 80 percent of the harm reduction achieved by utility filtering, at zero runtime cost, and cost at most 1 point in the store-off setting. P5: removing content-overlapping task clauses changes the interaction by less than one third of the read-policy removal; if the content mediator dominates, the archived substitution account wins and this claim is refuted. Name: order_randomized_leakage_audit
Title: Solved It Before: Stream-Order Randomization Shows That Experience-Memory Gains on Agent Benchmarks Concentrate on Tasks With a Near-Duplicate Solved Predecessor
Short Hypothesis: On the task-execution benchmarks used to evaluate agent experience memory (ALFWorld, WebShop, and the streaming protocols of ReMem, ReMe and Dynamic Cheatsheet), the reported gain of an experience store over a memoryless agent is concentrated in test tasks that already have a near-duplicate solved episode in the store (same task template, same object/receptacle class, same or similar scene); for tasks without such a predecessor the gain falls inside the run-to-run noise floor. Randomizing the order of the task stream turns 'has a near-duplicate solved predecessor' into a within-task randomized treatment, giving a causal estimate of the leakage share, and a non-LLM nearest-neighbour trajectory replay reproduces most of the gain. Task-order variance in streaming evaluation is therefore not noise: it is the leakage effect in disguise.
Related Work: ExpeL (Zhao et al., 2023) builds its ALFWorld store from training-split episodes and evaluates on the unseen split, which shares all six task templates and most object/receptacle classes; it reports no store-to-test distance analysis. ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696), ReMem's streaming benchmark (arXiv:2511.20857) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952) evaluate over a task stream and report continual-improvement curves without order permutation or predecessor accounting. SkillEvolBench (arXiv:2605.24117) organizes tasks into families with shared latent procedures and finds raw-trajectory reuse often beats distilled skills, which is what near-duplicate lookup predicts, but does not stratify gains by store-test distance; 'When Continual Learning Moves to Memory' (arXiv:2604.27003) frames experience reuse as a transfer-forgetting trade-off at retrieval without a distance-aware split. StreamMemBench (ICLR 2026) shows retrieval and application accuracy diverge on a QA stream with evidence boundaries; MemDelta (arXiv:2606.29914) varies one component at a time on LongMemEval-S and recommends fixing embedders and stratifying by model family; both are QA and neither randomizes order or audits leakage from an inference-time store. The benchmark-contamination literature (arXiv:2601.19334, arXiv:2603.21636, arXiv:2311.01964) treats pretraining leakage; 'Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection' (arXiv:2606.28374) enforces held-out selection for evolved configurations but not a distance-aware split. Scaffold splits in molecular ML and temporal splits in recommender evaluation are the methodological precedents for the leave-neighbourhood-out curve proposed here.
Abstract: Experience-memory papers report gains on ALFWorld, WebShop and streaming task suites as evidence that an agent generalizes from past episodes. These benchmarks are template-generated: thousands of tasks share a task type, a target object class, a receptacle and a floorplan, so a store built from training or earlier-stream episodes frequently contains a solved episode that differs from the test task only in scene or object identity. No published evaluation reports how much of the gain sits on such near-duplicates. We introduce two reporting instruments. (1) A leave-neighbourhood-out (LNO) curve: the paired memory-minus-memoryless success delta as a function of the minimum structural distance d between the test task and any stored episode (d=0 exact task, d=1 same type/object/receptacle in another scene, d=2 same type and receptacle, d=3 same type only, d=4 different type), with store size held constant by matched random removal. (2) An order-randomization estimator for streaming protocols: the stream is shuffled R times, each task is evaluated prequentially in every order, and the effect of 'a near-duplicate solved predecessor exists at evaluation time' is estimated within task across orders with task, order and seed as crossed random effects. We apply both to raw-trajectory retrieval, ExpeL-style insights and a ReMe-style distilled procedural store on 1,465 ALFWorld tasks and WebShop, with the 27B dense and 120B MoE backbones already served in this program plus Qwen3-8B. A nearest-neighbour replay control (single closest solved trajectory by template distance, no reflection, no embedding retriever) bounds how much of each system's gain is lookup. We predict that the d<=1 stratum carries most of the gain, that d>=3 deltas are inside the noise floor for raw trajectories, that conditioning on predecessor counts removes most between-order variance, and that de-duplicated stream orders flatten the continual-improvement curve. The outcome that would refute us, insights retaining their gain at d>=3, would itself be the first clean demonstration of abstraction transfer under a leakage-controlled split. Either way the LNO curve becomes a required artifact for memory claims on template-generated benchmarks.
Experiments: (1) Distance metric: for ALFWorld compute the exact structural distance from the task's PDDL fields (type, object class, receptacle, floorplan); for WebShop use category and attribute-set overlap; report an embedding-distance version as a robustness check. (2) Split protocol on ALFWorld: build each store (raw trajectories; ExpeL insights; ReMe-style distilled records with LLM-judge validation) from a training pool of successful and failed episodes generated by the same backbone; evaluate on the remaining tasks (target 1,465 minus pool, stratified by type) with k in {1,3,7}; then LNO at d in {0,1,2,3,4}, each with a matched-size random-removal control so store size is constant; 2 decoding seeds per (task, config). (3) Streaming protocol: a 400-task stratified subsample shuffled into R=10-20 orders; prequential evaluation with the store growing after each task; record for every (task, order) the number and minimum distance of solved predecessors; fit success ~ memory x predecessor-stratum with crossed random effects for task, order and seed; also run a greedy de-duplicated order (no task follows a d<=1 predecessor) and an adversarial order (near-duplicates first). (4) Lookup bound: nearest-neighbour replay at k=1 with the closest solved trajectory by structural distance, no LLM reflection. (5) Replicate on WebShop (500 test tasks, 300-task stream) and on Qwen3-8B to test backbone dependence. Budget: roughly 25k episodes for the split protocol and 15-25k for the streaming protocol, within days on 4xA100 with batched vLLM serving.
Baselines and Ablations: Memoryless agent; memoryless agent with a fixed hand-written instruction; memoryless with random-token padding matched to the injected length (load control); relevance-matched decoy injection (a d=2 item deliberately substituted for the retrieved d<=1 item: same type and receptacle, wrong object) to separate near-duplicate content from load and from topical relevance; nearest-neighbour replay (k=1, no reflection); raw-trajectory retrieval at k=1,3,7; ExpeL insights; ReMe-style distilled store; LNO at each d with matched-size random removal; random order vs de-duplicated order vs adversarial order; two backbones per environment.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: On the split protocol, the paired memory-minus-memoryless delta in the d<=1 stratum is at least three times the delta in the d>=3 stratum, and the d>=3 delta's 95% CI includes zero for raw-trajectory retrieval. P2: In the streaming protocol the within-task effect of a near-duplicate solved predecessor explains at least 50% of the aggregate memory gain, and conditioning on predecessor counts reduces between-order variance of the aggregate gain by at least 50%. P3: Nearest-neighbour replay at k=1 captures at least 70% of the full system's gain for raw trajectories and at least 50% for distilled stores. P4: The continual-improvement slope over stream position is inside the null-replicate slope band under the de-duplicated order but not under random order. Refutation: if any store retains at least 50% of its gain at d>=3 (falsifies the leakage account for that store), or if the predecessor effect explains less than 25% of the gain, or if replay captures less than 40%, the hypothesis fails.
Measurement and Noise Control: All comparisons are paired by task and decoding seed; primary test is McNemar on paired success with mixed-effects logistic models for stratum-by-memory interactions and crossed random effects (task, order, seed). Minimum detectable effect is pre-registered from the pilot discordance rate: with roughly 1,300 paired tasks and 2 seeds, a discordance rate of 0.25 gives an MDE near 2.5 points; per-stratum MDEs are reported with stratum n and strata are fixed before the confirmatory run. Null replicates (memoryless vs memoryless under a second seed, and the same store re-scored) calibrate the noise floor and the null slope band for continual-improvement curves. Store size is held constant across LNO levels by matched random removal; decoding temperature is fixed and seeds are controlled per (task, config). Bootstrap over tasks (and over orders for the streaming protocol) gives CIs on stratum deltas, on the explained-variance share and on the replay ratio. Backbone and environment are treated as replication factors, not pooled.

Risk Factors and Limitations: ALFWorld's PDDL template structure makes near-duplicates unusually easy to define, so the size of the leakage share may be benchmark-specific; WebShop provides a second, less structured case and the embedding-distance version tests sensitivity to the metric. Removing neighbourhoods shrinks the store; the matched-size random-removal control addresses size but not diversity, which is reported separately. Prequential streaming does not match ReMe's offline pool construction exactly, so the split protocol is the primary test for ReMe-style stores. If insights transfer at d>=3, the headline changes from 'memory gains are leakage' to 'raw trajectories leak, insights transfer', which is still a reporting standard but a weaker critique. Name: memory_surrogate_validity
Title: Good Memory, Wrong Endpoint: Retrieval Recall, LLM-Judge Quality and Admission F1 Do Not Rank Agent Experience Memories by Execution Success
Short Hypothesis: The metrics used to develop and compare agent experience memories - recall/MRR of labeled-relevant episodes, LLM-judge quality or utility scores of stored items, admission-gate precision/recall as in A-MAC, and memory reward-model scores - are surrogate endpoints whose validity for the true endpoint, task-execution success, has never been measured. Across a pre-registered family of memory configurations that spans the surrogates' ranges (retriever, k, item form, admission gate, backbone) the surrogate-endpoint rank correlation is weak (Kendall tau below 0.5 after correcting for the endpoint's own test-retest reliability), recall is non-monotone with execution beyond small k, no single surrogate explains more than half of the treatment effect (Freedman's proportion explained), and selecting the configuration by the best surrogate yields a system indistinguishable from the memoryless control. A cheap execution-anchored probe (agreement of the first three memory-conditioned actions with a verified success trajectory) is a valid surrogate at about a tenth of the episode cost.
Related Work: A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549) reports precision-recall of a five-factor admission gate without linking it to downstream accuracy; ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) validates and prunes items with an LLM judge and lists judge reliance as a limitation; MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192) learns per-item utilities as the selection signal; the memory reward-model benchmark (arXiv:2601.11969) scores RMs without testing transfer to downstream performance. 'Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents' (arXiv:2608.00017) shows self-graded rewards inflate incorrect episodes at write time (the Echo Gap) and RoMeRL (arXiv:2608.02508) names a memory-reward trap; both concern reward signals inside a self-improvement loop, not the validity of the metrics used to select and compare memory configurations. MemoryArena (arXiv:2602.16313) and LongMemEval-V2 (arXiv:2605.12493) observe that QA-benchmark saturation does not carry to action tasks, a cross-benchmark observation; Task2Quiz (arXiv:2601.09503) shows the converse, that task success poorly indicates environment understanding. 'Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory' (arXiv:2603.02473) finds retrieval choice dominates write strategy on QA memory without validating any surrogate. The closest methodological neighbours are 'When Retrieval Metrics Mislead' (arXiv:2606.23937), which finds exact-match clause recall underestimates downstream policy utility in a tool-use policy-retrieval benchmark, 'The Recall Trap' (arXiv:2608.14838, surfaced by web search, unverified on S2/HF), where a recall-maximizing code-context configuration lowered SWE-bench Verified resolve rate, and 'What Survives Into Context' (arXiv:2607.00725), where an answer-in-context diagnostic beats document recall for multi-hop RAG; none covers an agent's own experience memory, judge or admission surrogates, or a formal surrogate-validity criterion with selection regret. Prentice's and Freedman's surrogate-endpoint criteria from clinical trials supply the analysis framework.
Abstract: Agent experience memories are tuned, pruned and compared with proxies: recall of relevant episodes, an LLM judge's quality score, admission-gate F1 on curated records, or a reward model's rating. Papers report these proxies as if they measured what the memory is for, which is to raise task-execution success. We treat them as surrogate endpoints and measure their validity directly. On ALFWorld (1,465 tasks) and WebShop we build one pool of successful and failed episodes and a pre-registered family of 20 memory configurations crossing retriever (BM25, dense, structural oracle, random, adversarial-nearest-wrong), k in {1,3,7}, item form (raw trajectory, insight), admission gate (none, LLM judge, five-factor A-MAC-style, self-consistency) and two open backbones. For each configuration we compute every surrogate and the paired execution-success delta against the memoryless control over the same tasks and seeds. Validity is reported three ways: Kendall tau between surrogate and endpoint across configurations, attenuation-corrected by the endpoint's test-retest reliability from null replicates; Freedman's proportion of treatment effect explained; and selection regret, the endpoint loss from choosing the configuration the surrogate prefers. Adversarial items that are plausible but task-wrong test whether judges can see harm. We expect recall to be non-monotone with execution beyond k=1, judge scores to be blind to harm, gate F1 to misrank gates, and selection by surrogate to land within noise of no memory. As a constructive result we validate a prefix-agreement probe, the agreement of the first three memory-conditioned actions with a verified success trajectory, which must reach tau at least 0.7 to be recommended. The outcome that refutes the thesis, any existing surrogate reaching corrected tau at least 0.8 with proportion explained at least 0.8, would equally be worth publishing because it would license the field's current practice.
Experiments: (1) Pool and labels: generate a pool of successful and failed episodes on ALFWorld training tasks with the 27B backbone; derive two relevance labelings for each test task: structural (same type/object/receptacle) and counterfactual (whether injecting that single item as k=1 changes success, computed on a 200-task subset with 2 seeds). (2) Configuration family: 20 pre-registered configurations crossing retriever, k, item form, gate and backbone (Qwen3-8B and the 27B dense model); no configuration is added after the confirmatory run starts. (3) Surrogates per configuration: recall@k and MRR against each labeling; mean LLM-judge quality of injected items using two local judges (the 120B MoE and the 27B); admission-gate precision/recall/F1 against planted wrong, obsolete and off-task records inserted into the write stream; reward-model score using a local RM prompt; the proposed prefix-agreement probe. (4) Endpoint: paired execution success vs memoryless on a 600-task stratified evaluation set, 2 seeds; WebShop replication with 12 configurations on 500 tasks. (5) Analysis: Kendall tau and Spearman rho with bootstrap CIs over tasks and configurations; attenuation correction using the endpoint's test-retest tau from re-scoring the same configurations under new seeds; Freedman's proportion explained via logistic models with and without the surrogate; selection regret; surrogate-optimal k vs endpoint-optimal k. (6) Probe validation: fit and validate the prefix-agreement probe on disjoint halves of the configuration family. Budget: about 24k ALFWorld episodes plus 6k WebShop episodes and roughly 3k prefix-probe runs, feasible in days on 4xA100.
Baselines and Ablations: Memoryless control; memoryless with random-token padding matched to injected length; oracle-relevance retrieval at k=1,3,7 (recall fixed at 1 while k varies, isolating the recall-monotonicity question); adversarial-nearest-wrong retrieval (high judge score, task-wrong items) as a harm-visibility test for the judge and RM surrogates; gate on/off with the same retriever to isolate the gate's contribution; single-judge vs two-judge scoring; structural vs counterfactual relevance labels; top-half-only correlation to guard against a family dominated by bad configurations; probe trained on one half of the family and tested on the other.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: Corrected Kendall tau between recall@k and the execution delta across configurations is below 0.5, and oracle-relevance retrieval at k=7 does not beat oracle retrieval at k=1 (paired difference inside the MDE), so recall is non-monotone with the endpoint. P2: LLM-judge item quality has corrected tau below 0.3, and adversarial plausible-but-wrong items score within 0.3 SD of correct items while lowering success by at least 5 points. P3: Admission F1 against planted records has corrected tau below 0.5 with the gated-minus-ungated execution delta, and at least one gate with higher F1 yields lower execution success than a gate with lower F1. P4: The configuration chosen by the best existing surrogate loses at least 3 points to the endpoint-optimal configuration and is not distinguishable from the memoryless control. P5: The prefix-agreement probe reaches corrected tau at least 0.7 and proportion explained at least 0.6 at no more than 15% of episode cost. Refutation: any existing surrogate reaching corrected tau at least 0.8 and proportion explained at least 0.8, or the probe failing tau 0.7 on the held-out half, falsifies the respective claim.
Measurement and Noise Control: The endpoint is paired by task and seed against the memoryless control; the test-retest reliability of the endpoint (same configuration, new seeds) is measured first and sets the ceiling for any surrogate's correlation, which is reported both raw and attenuation-corrected. Null replicates calibrate the spread of deltas under no treatment, and the MDE is pre-registered (about 3 points paired at 600 tasks x 2 seeds with discordance 0.25). Correlation CIs come from a two-level bootstrap over tasks within configurations and over configurations. The configuration family, labelings, judges, gates and thresholds are fixed before the confirmatory run; surrogate scores are computed once and frozen before endpoints are unblinded. Judge prompts and RM prompts are fixed and reported; judge stochasticity is averaged over 3 samples per item. Backbone and environment are replication factors, reported separately.

Name: amortization_horizon_ranking_flip
Title: Cheaper Than What? The Cost Definition and the Amortization Horizon Decide Whether an 8B Agent With Memory Beats a 14B Agent Without It
Short Hypothesis: Published memory-versus-scale claims (ReMe: Qwen3-8B with memory reaches Pass@4 55.03 against 54.65 for memoryless Qwen3-14B on BFCL-V3/AppWorld) and memory-versus-memory rankings are functions of two undeclared parameters: the cost definition (prompt tokens, generated tokens, GPU-seconds, wall-clock at fixed hardware and batching) and the amortization horizon N over which write-path cost (reflection, distillation, LLM-judge validation, pruning) is spread. Under GPU-seconds per solved task at the horizon implicit in the source papers' evaluation-set sizes, the memoryless larger model dominates the smaller model with memory; the memory system wins only beyond a break-even horizon N* that we estimate with a confidence interval; and the ranking among raw-trajectory, distilled and consolidated stores reverses between token cost and GPU-seconds because write-heavy designs move cost into construction. The 0.38-point Pass@4 margin itself lies inside the seed-to-seed spread.
Related Work: ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) reports the memory-scaling claim on BFCL-V3 and AppWorld with Qwen3-8B/14B/32B without cost accounting or seeds. AMA-Bench (arXiv:2602.22769) folds amortized construction tokens into a single average-per-kilotoken column at its own query count, fixing one cost definition and one horizon; 'Compact-Memory LLM Agents' (arXiv:2609.04915) does the same with amortized organization cost. 'Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications' (arXiv:2606.06448) profiles write-path versus read-path cost and finds construction-heavy paradigms move most energy into construction, but reports cost attribution without quality-linked rankings. MemDelta (arXiv:2606.29914) recommends reporting write-path cost before attributing gains to architecture, on LongMemEval-S QA, without varying the horizon or adding a cost-matched larger backbone. 'Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction' (arXiv:2607.12161) shows for coding-agent context reduction that success-adjusted billed cost ranks methods differently from token counts because prompt caching dominates; it does not treat memory systems, amortized write paths or memory-versus-scale claims. BudgetMem (arXiv:2602.06025) routes queries across budget tiers of runtime memory; 'Inference-Time Distillation' (arXiv:2512.02543) shifts the cost-accuracy frontier on ALFWorld and AppWorld with dynamic in-context learning and self-consistency cascades and is the natural matched-compute memoryless control. The cost-aware pipeline of arXiv:2608.04843 leaves ranking sensitivity to the cost definition untested; Capability-Preserving Evolution (arXiv:2605.09315), MEMO (arXiv:2603.09022) and Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) report accuracy without the cost of their loops. Dehghani et al.'s 'The Efficiency Misnomer' (2021) showed that FLOPs, parameters and throughput rank models differently; this proposal is the agent-memory analogue with the amortization horizon as an additional free parameter.
Abstract: Memory papers now claim that a small model with experience memory beats a larger model without it, and rank memory designs by accuracy alone or by prompt tokens at a fixed evaluation size. Both claims hide two choices: which cost is counted, and over how many future tasks the cost of building the memory is spread. We reimplement a ReMe-style distilled procedural store, raw-trajectory retrieval and ExpeL-style insights for Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B (plus this program's 27B dense and 120B MoE backbones) on ALFWorld (1,465 tasks) and the public multi-turn subset of BFCL-V3, all served on one 4xA100 node with metered prompt tokens, generated tokens, server-side GPU-seconds and wall-clock under two batching regimes, with write-path and read-path cost separated. For each system we trace the cost-quality frontier as a function of the amortization horizon N in {100, 500, 1k, 5k, 20k} and under each cost definition, add a cost-matched larger memoryless backbone and a matched-compute memoryless control (self-consistency cascades), and report Kendall tau between system rankings across cost definitions and horizons together with the break-even horizon N* and its bootstrap CI. We predict that the larger memoryless model has lower GPU-seconds per solved task than the smaller model with memory for every N up to 1,000; that N* exceeds the evaluation-set sizes of the source papers, so the published claim sits on the wrong side of its own break-even; that the memory-system ranking flips between token and GPU-second accounting and between N=100 and N=20k; and that the 0.38-point margin is inside the null-replicate spread. If the small model with memory dominates under GPU-seconds at N at most 500 and the margin survives four seeds, the thesis fails and the published claim is strengthened. The deliverable is a reporting standard: cost-quality frontiers indexed by horizon, with the cost definition and the cost-matched larger backbone declared.
Experiments: (1) Systems: ReMe-style dynamic procedural memory (using the released Memory-Management-Kit where possible), raw-trajectory retrieval and ExpeL-style insights, each at the k used in its source and at k=1,3,7. (2) Backbones: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B for the ReMe replication; the program's 27B dense and 120B MoE for the memory-system ranking; all on one 4xA100 node with vLLM. (3) Metering: per-request prompt and generated tokens, server-side GPU-seconds (request time x GPUs held), wall-clock under a latency regime (batch 1) and a throughput regime (saturated batch), each timing repeated 3 times to report a CV; write path (pool generation, distillation, judge validation, pruning, consolidation) and read path (retrieval and injected context) metered separately. (4) Quality: paired success on 1,465 ALFWorld tasks with 3-4 seeds per (task, config); BFCL-V3 multi-turn subset with Avg@4 and Pass@4 as in ReMe. (5) Frontier and rankings: for each cost definition and N compute cost per solved task, the frontier, N* where the memory system crosses the larger memoryless backbone, and Kendall tau between system rankings across (definition, N) pairs; bootstrap over tasks and seeds for CIs. (6) Controls: cost-matched larger memoryless backbone; matched-compute memoryless (self-consistency action voting at matched GPU-seconds, plus pass@n as an upper bound); random-token padding matched to the injected length to attribute read-path cost to prefill. Budget: roughly 30k ALFWorld episodes plus about 6k BFCL-V3 evaluations across systems, backbones and seeds, feasible in days.
Baselines and Ablations: Memoryless small backbone; memoryless larger backbone at equal or lower GPU-seconds per task; matched-compute memoryless small backbone (self-consistency action voting; pass@n upper bound); memoryless with random-token padding matched to injected length; three memory systems at k=1,3,7; write-path components toggled (judge validation on/off, pruning on/off) to attribute write cost; two batching regimes; two cost definitions per axis (tokens vs GPU-seconds; per task vs per solved task); horizons N in {100, 500, 1k, 5k, 20k}; 3-4 seeds.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: Under GPU-seconds per solved task including read-path context, memoryless Qwen3-14B beats Qwen3-8B with ReMe-style memory at every N at most 1,000, and the Pass@4 margin (0.38 points as published) lies inside the four-seed null-replicate spread on our replication. P2: The break-even horizon N* at which the memory system dominates the larger memoryless model has a 95% CI whose lower bound exceeds the evaluation-set sizes of the source papers (hundreds of tasks). P3: The ranking of the three memory systems changes between prompt-token and GPU-second accounting (Kendall tau at most 0.33) and again between N=100 and N=20k. P4: At least half of the memory system's read-path GPU-second overhead is reproduced by the random-token padding control, so it is prefill load, not retrieval or generation. Refutation: if 8B with memory dominates 14B memoryless under GPU-seconds at N at most 500 with the margin surviving four seeds, or if rankings are stable across cost definitions and horizons (tau at least 0.8), the thesis is false.
Measurement and Noise Control: Quality is paired by task and seed with McNemar and mixed-effects logistic models; 3-4 seeds per configuration; MDE pre-registered at about 2 points paired for 1,465 tasks x 3 seeds. Null replicates (same configuration, new seeds) give the spread against which the 0.38-point margin is judged. Cost is metered server-side with hardware, serving stack, batching policy and quantization fixed and reported; timing is repeated 3 times and its CV reported; GPU-seconds are reported under both batching regimes because rankings may depend on the regime. Frontiers, N* and ranking taus get bootstrap CIs over tasks and seeds. Cost definitions, horizons, systems and controls are fixed before the confirmatory run; write-path costs are logged per operation so amortization can be recomputed for any N by readers.

Name: need_blind_compaction_audit
Title: Need-Blind by Construction: A Counterfactual Audit of What Agent Context Compaction Drops, and Why Summary Fidelity Does Not Predict Task Success
Short Hypothesis: The task-success loss that context compaction causes in long-horizon tool-use agents is concentrated in a small set of load-bearing history items (identifiable by counterfactual masking of the history), LLM summarizers retain load-bearing items at no higher rate than non-load-bearing ones (they are need-blind), and therefore load-bearing retention, not compression ratio or summary fidelity, predicts the success loss; a pinning rule derived from counterfactual need labels on disjoint task types recovers most of the loss at matched tokens, whereas same-size recency or salience pinning does not.
Related Work: Governance Decay (arXiv:2606.22528) is the only measurement of a specific fact class silently dropped by compaction; it plants governance constraints adversarially, measures only their survival, and fixes it with Constraint Pinning. The Compaction Cliff / Knowledge Triage (arXiv:2608.22752, Aug 2026) routes knowledge-base lines through type-specific retention policies but has no ground truth of which lines later steps needed. ACON (arXiv:2510.00615, ICML 2026) optimizes compression guidelines from paired full-vs-compressed failures but never reports what was dropped per item. Memex (arXiv:2603.04257) notes that missing indices silently derail later reasoning but does not quantify it. Structured eviction (arXiv:2606.11213), parallel-block compaction (arXiv:2605.23296), SelfCompact (arXiv:2606.23525) and CompactionRL (arXiv:2607.05378) report only end-task success. Masking stale observations (arXiv:2606.00408) uses masking as an intervention with a regime map, not as an audit instrument. None of these builds a per-item need ground truth on real agent traces, tests whether summarizers are need-sensitive, or tests whether generic fidelity metrics carry any information about downstream success.
Abstract: Every compaction scheme for long-horizon agents (LLM summarization, deterministic eviction, indexed archives, parallel blocks, learned compaction) is evaluated by end-task success, so what a locally plausible summary discards, and how often the discarded item is one a later step needs, is unmeasured beyond the single governance-constraint case. We propose a counterfactual audit: for reference episodes solved with full context, we mask each pre-boundary history item individually at a fixed compaction boundary and measure, first by teacher-forced action divergence at every later step and then by paired stochastic continuations, whether removing that item changes the agent's later actions and success. Items whose removal lowers continuation success are load-bearing. We then apply six compaction families at the same boundary and measure each family's retention of load-bearing versus non-load-bearing items (entailment judge validated against human annotation), its generic fidelity (ROUGE, LLM-judge faithfulness, compression ratio) and its paired downstream success loss. The central claim is that LLM summarizers are need-blind: their retention rate for load-bearing items equals their retention rate for everything else, so their success loss is explained by load-bearing drop events and not by fidelity metrics. As a constructive test, we learn a type-level pinning rule from need labels on one split of ALFWorld task types and apply it on held-out types at matched total tokens, against random, recency, salience and task-statement-only pinning and against an oracle that pins the counterfactual load-bearing set. We run 8B, 27B-class dense and 120B MoE open-weight backbones on ALFWorld (primary) and WebShop, with paired designs, null replicates and pre-registered thresholds.
Experiments: Setup: ReAct scaffold; ALFWorld (1,465 tasks, six task types) as primary, WebShop as secondary; backbones Qwen3-8B, a 27B-class dense model and gpt-oss-120B served locally with vLLM prefix caching. Compaction boundary t* is the first step at which history exceeds a token budget B (three budgets), or a fixed step for short episodes. Phase 1, need labels: take reference episodes that succeed with full context; for each pre-boundary item i (observation, action, error message; the task statement is excluded), build the teacher-forced dependency matrix D[i,s] = 1 if replacing item i by an [omitted] marker changes the greedy action at later reference step s (one forward pass per (i,s), prefix-cached). For every item with any divergence, run n=4 stochastic continuations from t* with item i masked and compare with n=4 unmasked continuations; label load-bearing if the paired success drop exceeds a pre-registered threshold. Record item type (object-location observation, receptacle open/closed state, failed action plus error, navigation, inventory change, sub-goal completion). Target about 600 boundary episodes per backbone. Phase 2, audit: at the same boundaries apply (a) backbone self-summary with a ReSum-style prompt, (b) summary with an ACON-style optimized guideline, (c) recency truncation, (d) dependency-aware structured eviction reimplemented from arXiv:2606.11213, (e) indexed summary plus external archive with dereference (prompted Memex analogue, dereference tokens counted), (f) parallel-block compaction. For each, compute retention R_LB and R_nonLB by an entailment judge (200 items double-annotated for kappa), generic fidelity metrics, working-context tokens, manager decode tokens, and paired continuation success versus full context. Phase 3, need-aware pinning: fit a type-level rule (pin item types whose load-bearing probability exceeds p) on task-type split A; on split B pin those items verbatim outside the summary with the summary budget reduced so total tokens match; compare with random, recency, LLM-salience and task-statement-only pinning at the same token count, and with the oracle pin of the counterfactual load-bearing set.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: full context (upper reference), recency truncation, LLM self-summary, ACON-guideline summary, structured eviction, indexed archive with dereference, parallel-block compaction, SelfCompact-style agent-chosen compaction timing. Pinning controls at matched total tokens: random, recency, LLM-salience, task-statement-only (Constraint Pinning analogue), oracle load-bearing pin. Ablations: boundary position (early, mid, late), token budget (three levels), teacher-forced versus rollout-confirmed labels (agreement rate), string-match versus entailment-judge retention, per-item-type analysis, cross-backbone transfer of the type rule (rule learned on 8B applied to 27B and 120B), and WebShop replication of Phases 1 and 2.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: load-bearing items are at most 20 percent of pre-boundary items, and in episodes where every load-bearing item survives compaction the paired success loss is indistinguishable from zero (95 percent CI includes 0), so at least 60 percent of the summarizer's total success loss occurs in episodes with at least one load-bearing drop. P2 (need-blindness): for the LLM summarizer, R_LB minus R_nonLB lies within plus or minus 0.05 (TOST equivalence); if R_LB exceeds R_nonLB by more than 0.15 the need-blindness claim is falsified and summarizers are need-sensitive. P3: in a per-episode logistic model of success loss, R_LB reaches AUC of at least 0.70 and adding ROUGE, compression ratio and judge faithfulness yields no significant likelihood-ratio improvement; if fidelity metrics predict as well as R_LB the claim fails. P4: type-rule pinning on held-out task types recovers at least 50 percent of the full-context-minus-summary gap at matched tokens, while random and recency pinning recover under 20 percent; if type-rule pinning does not beat salience pinning, need labels add nothing over an LLM's own importance judgment. P5: structured eviction and the indexed archive have higher R_LB than summarization, and their success advantage over summarization shrinks to within the noise floor once dereference and manager tokens are matched (cost-accounted comparison).
Measurement and Noise Control: All conditions continue from the identical boundary state (same prefix, same environment instance, same seed), so comparisons are paired at the episode level and tested with McNemar; per-episode bootstrap CIs; mixed-effects logistic regression with task-type random effects. Noise floor: two independent full-context continuation sets per backbone (null replicate) define the run-to-run band; any effect inside that band is reported as null. Minimum detectable effect: with 600 paired boundary episodes and an expected discordance rate near 0.2, the design detects about 4 to 5 points at alpha 0.05 and power 0.8; equivalence tests use a pre-registered margin of 0.05 on retention. Judge validation: 200 retention judgments double-annotated, kappa reported, string-match sensitivity analysis. Thresholds for load-bearing labels, the retention margin, and the pinning recovery target are pre-registered before the confirmatory run; Phase 1 label thresholds are chosen on a 100-episode pilot excluded from confirmatory analysis.

Channel WebSearch (closest method), query: 'Constraint Pinning governance decay context compaction agent summarization' -> only 2606.22528 and commentary. Channel WebSearch (closest method 2), query: 'ACON context compression guidelines long-horizon agent failure analysis optimize natural language' -> arXiv:2510.00615 (ICML 2026), no per-item loss audit. Channel s2cli (mechanism), query: 'counterfactual masking history items load-bearing context compaction agent information loss later steps' -> arXiv:2606.00408 (masking stale observations as intervention, regime map), arXiv:2606.11213 (structured eviction), remaining hits off-topic (KV cache, video diffusion); no counterfactual need audit found. Channel s2cli (closest method), query: 'dependency-aware eviction typed episodes agent context budget summarization lossiness' -> 2606.11213 plus KV-cache eviction papers (MemDecay 2607.10582, TokenPilot 2606.17016, IndexMem 2605.25475); none audits need. Channel s2cli, query: 'summary faithfulness metric predicts downstream agent task success context compaction quality evaluation' -> SelfCompact 2606.23525, CompactionRL 2607.05378, arXiv:2603.17104 (faithfulness loss in coding agents with emerging specs), arXiv:2607.14275; none relates fidelity metrics to per-item need. Conclusion: no collision on the counterfactual need audit or the need-blindness claim; Knowledge Triage is the closest constructive neighbour and is positioned as an untested prior for the type rule.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Teacher-forced divergence can over-label (an action changes without changing success), so rollout confirmation is mandatory and adds cost; load-bearing labels are policy-dependent, so a rule learned on one backbone may not transfer (P5 and the cross-backbone ablation make this a reported result rather than an assumption). ALFWorld histories are short, so compaction must be forced with small budgets, and WebShop histories are dominated by page text; the audit generalizes to coding or web agents only by analogy. The entailment judge is itself an LLM and can miss paraphrased retention; human validation bounds this. If summarizers turn out to be need-sensitive (P2 fails), the paper becomes a negative result about where the loss actually sits, which is still informative but weaker.
Addresses gap: G11: it replaces end-task-only reporting with a per-item, need-conditioned measurement of what each compaction family discards, and tests whether the silent-drop phenomenon is general (need-blindness) rather than a governance-constraint special case.
Not a restatement of: Nearest prior-result bullet: 'Injection volume, not memory content, was the causal lever' concerns how many cross-task items are injected; this idea concerns which within-task items are removed and shows that a small need-defined subset, not volume, carries the loss. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2606.22528 measures survival of planted governance constraints only; this idea builds need labels for every history item on organic traces, tests need-blindness against non-load-bearing items, and shows that generic fidelity metrics do not predict success loss. Nearest archived idea: memory_budget_confound claims token volume explains cross-task memory harm; this idea claims token volume is not what matters inside a task and identifies the load-bearing set.

Name: state_load_not_length
Title: State Count, Not Token Count: Dissociating Cumulative State Load from Context Length on Real Agent Traces, and Which Context Manager Closes Which
Short Hypothesis: On real environment traces, long-horizon agent failure scales with the number of state changes the agent must carry (cumulative state load), not with context length at matched tokens; the length-alone effect established on static inputs is below the noise floor at the lengths agents actually reach; a deterministic state scratchpad closes the state-load effect at a fraction of the tokens, LLM summarization closes it only partially because it drops the needed relocation, and eviction converts it into a re-exploration cost.
Related Work: Three diagnostic accounts of long-context failure exist, all established off agent traces: length alone hurts despite perfect retrieval (arXiv:2510.05381, EMNLP, static RULER-style inputs); cumulative working-memory load drives difficulty (WMF-AM, arXiv:2603.27343, scratchpad-free arithmetic probe, K in 3,5,7, 28 models, with a correlational 10-task ReAct battery tau 0.595 and a load-shift pilot the authors call confounded); and hard distractors cause a sharply nonlinear drop (arXiv:2605.10828, retrieved documents). Proactive Memory Agent (arXiv:2607.08716) names behavioral state decay and injects reminders but does not dissociate causes; LongHorizon-Harness (arXiv:2608.01964) keeps task state outside context without ablation; ACON (arXiv:2510.00615), Memex (arXiv:2603.04257), LongSeeker (arXiv:2605.05191) and Memory-as-Action (arXiv:2510.12635) manage context without measuring which of the three loads they remove. No paper manipulates state load and length independently inside a real environment or reports which manager closes which load.
Abstract: Diagnostic findings about why long contexts fail (length alone, cumulative working-memory load, hard distractors) were obtained on static inputs, scratchpad-free probes or retrieved documents, so whether they predict long-horizon agent failure on real tool-use traces, or whether any context-management scheme closes them, is unknown. We build a factorial manipulation inside a real environment: before each ALFWorld target task, a scripted controller executes a prefix of K admissible actions in the same environment instance, so the observations are real and the world state actually changes. Prefix types are matched on token count: STATE-NEEDLE (K relocations, one of which moves the target object or closes its receptacle, so the task later requires the remembered fact), STATE-IRRELEVANT (K relocations of objects the task never needs), DISTRACTOR (K relocations of objects semantically similar to the target), LENGTH (K non-state-changing examine/look/inventory actions of the same token count), and none. Each account predicts a distinct signature: the length account predicts that all prefixes hurt equally; the cumulative-load account predicts that STATE-IRRELEVANT hurts and scales with K; the needle-retrieval account predicts only STATE-NEEDLE hurts; the hard-distractor account predicts a concave DISTRACTOR curve. We then run context managers on the same prefixes: full context, LLM summary at the boundary, a deterministic world-state scratchpad parsed from observations, an LLM-maintained scratchpad, recency eviction of the prefix, an indexed archive with dereference, and a proactive reminder agent, with every manager's own tokens counted. Backbones are 8B, 27B-class and 120B MoE open-weight models; ScienceWorld replicates the prefix design. Paired designs, null replicates and pre-registered minimum detectable effects separate the effects from run-to-run noise.
Experiments: Environment: ALFWorld (primary), ScienceWorld (secondary) with a scripted prefix controller that issues admissible commands and records real observations; the agent (ReAct) starts with the prefix history in context. Factors: prefix type in {none, LENGTH, STATE-IRRELEVANT, STATE-NEEDLE, DISTRACTOR}, K in {4, 8, 16}, with token counts matched within 5 percent by padding LENGTH prefixes with additional examine actions. Target set: 400 held-out tasks stratified over the six task types, two seeds each, so about 800 paired episodes per cell, roughly 12 cells per backbone for the diagnostic phase. Managers (applied at the prefix/task boundary and again whenever the budget is exceeded): (a) full context; (b) backbone self-summary (ReSum-style); (c) deterministic world-state scratchpad (object to location, receptacle open/closed, inventory) built by rule-based parsing of observations, replacing the prefix; (d) LLM-maintained scratchpad updated per step; (e) recency eviction of the prefix; (f) indexed summary plus archive with dereference; (g) proactive reminder agent as in arXiv:2607.08716. Outcome measures: success, steps to success, first-divergence step, whether the manager output mentions the needed relocation (STATE-NEEDLE cells), working-context and manager tokens, wall time. Exploratory link to the probe: run WMF-AM on each backbone and correlate probe score with the STATE-IRRELEVANT slope across backbones (descriptive with 3 to 6 backbones).
