Name: opposite_sided_failure_under_shift
Title: Stale in Context, Eroded in Weights: In-Context and Parametric Experience Fail on Opposite Sides of a Distribution Shift, and Only One Failure Is Predictable from the Bank
Short Hypothesis: Over a task stream with a mid-stream conflicting shift that makes stored procedures wrong, an in-context experience store's post-shift dip is a read-path phenomenon whose size tracks the fraction of retrieved items that are pre-shift, that self-corrects once post-shift items dominate retrieval, and that costs pre-shift competence nothing; a parametric store built by continual LoRA on the same stream's successes shows no retrieval-fraction dependence, recovers as a function of update count, and erodes pre-shift competence monotonically with post-shift updates unless replay is paid. The two substrates fail on opposite sides of the shift, and the in-context failure is predictable from bank composition alone.
Related Work: When Continual Learning Moves to Memory (arXiv:2604.27003) shows old and new experience compete at retrieval and relocates the stability-plasticity dilemma to memory representation, without a parametric comparison, a shift with conflicting items, or recovery-time measurement. Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget? (arXiv:2605.09315) documents capability erosion across workflow, skill, model and memory channels and fixes it with Capability-Preserving Evolution, but does not run the memory and model channels on the same stream at matched preservation cost. UniMem (arXiv:2607.26017, TLDR only) routes between episodic storage and parametric consolidation on boundary-agnostic task streams as a system; Controlled Memory Interference (arXiv:2608.07622) manipulates relationships among stored memories inside the in-context substrate; arXiv:2606.04703 reports progressive capability collapse under multi-iteration experience internalization, parametric side only; Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated (arXiv:2605.12978) finds consolidated memories degrade while raw episodic trajectories hold up, in context only; AgentCL (arXiv:2606.02461) proposes controlled task streams for agent continual learning. The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608) and contextual drag (arXiv:2602.04288) characterize how injected conflicting items harm within an episode but not how an organically accumulated bank drags after a shift. MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192) utility scores and recency weighting are the read-time controls we test; replay and retained-task gates are the parametric ones.
Abstract: The parametric and in-context substrates for agent experience are each said to have a stability-plasticity problem, but they have never been run on the same stream with the same shift, and their failures are described with the same word, forgetting, although they cannot be the same mechanism: a bank forgets nothing and a LoRA retrieves nothing. We build a 600-episode ALFWorld stream with three phases (original rules, a conflicting shift, revert) and two shift types: an action-grammar change that makes stored trajectories syntactically wrong, and a benign task-mix change where stale items are merely irrelevant. On one 7B backbone we run six substrates through the same stream: in-context banks with raw, utility-scored and recency-weighted retrieval; continual LoRA on the stream's successes with and without a costed replay budget; and a no-memory control. Every 50 episodes a frozen probe evaluates each substrate on held-out tasks under current-phase rules and under phase-1 rules, paired across substrates. For the in-context substrate we log, per probe, the fraction of retrieved items that are pre-shift and label each item right, stale-wrong or irrelevant; for the parametric substrate we log update count and replay tokens. The pre-registered predictions are that the in-context dip is explained by stale fraction and vanishes when it is zero, that its recovery time is predictable from bank composition, that parametric erosion of phase-1 competence grows with post-shift updates while the bank's does not, and that the benign shift produces neither. The preservation cost of each substrate at matched recovery is reported in tokens and GPU-seconds. The result is the first opposite-sided characterization of the two substrates on the same stream and a bank-composition predictor for in-context drag.
Experiments: Backbone: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct primary; Gemma-3-27B replicate on the primary shift only. Stream: 600 episodes drawn from the 1,465 local ALFWorld tasks, type-stratified, ordered as phase 1 (episodes 1-200, original rules), phase 2 (201-400, shifted rules), phase 3 (401-600, original rules restored); stream order is re-sampled per seed (2 seeds). Shifts implemented as a thin wrapper over the ALFWorld action parser and observation text, no environment retraining: S1 conflicting grammar (e.g. take/put/go to renamed; old grammar returns an explicit invalid-action observation), S2 conflicting procedure (a new precondition such as opening any receptacle before taking, violations return a failure observation) as an extension, S3 benign task-mix change (phase 2 uses different task types, no rule change). Substrates, all on the same episode sequence and seeds: IC-raw (append every episode's trajectory with success label, retrieve k=3 by task-description similarity), IC-utility (MemRL-style per-item utility updated from episode reward, retrieval reranked by utility), IC-recency (recency-weighted retrieval), PM-plain (continual LoRA SFT on successful trajectories every 50 episodes, warm-started), PM-replay (same plus a fixed budget of earlier successes replayed each block, tokens costed), NONE (base every episode), plus IC-reset (bank cleared at each phase boundary) as the read-path upper bound and PM+IC-raw as the hybrid. Probes every 50 episodes: 40 held-out tasks under current-phase rules and 40 under phase-1 rules, one seed per probe point, substrate frozen, paired across substrates; 12 probe points x 80 tasks x 8 substrates x 2 shift types x 2 seeds is about 31,000 probe episodes, plus about 19,000 stream episodes, within a few days on four A100s. Logged per in-context probe episode: retrieved items with phase-of-origin and post hoc label (right, stale-wrong, irrelevant), stale fraction, and whether an invalid or failed action was copied from a retrieved item. Logged per parametric probe: cumulative post-shift updates, replay tokens, GPU-seconds. Name: stall_triggered_injection
Title: Retrieve When Stuck, Not When Starting: Injection Timing Sets the Sign of Experience Memory's Effect on Agent Traces, and a Two-Parameter Stall Trigger Matches a Learned Retrieval Policy
Short Hypothesis: For a fixed bank, fixed query, fixed k and the very same retrieved items, revealing the items at the first detected stall (repeated, invalid or state-preserving action) instead of at the first decision point flips the paired effect on ALFWorld from harm-or-null to gain, because at a stall the agent has its own trajectory evidence to arbitrate against wrong items whereas at entry it must comply blind. A swept two-parameter static stall trigger (stall length n, injection cap M) lands inside the seed-noise band of MemCon-style and RSCB-MC-style learned when-to-retrieve policies at lower token cost, and transfers across backbones (8B, 27B, 120B) and to WebShop without relearning, whereas the learned policies must be relearned.
Related Work: ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) retrieves once at task start and names context-aware retrieval as future work. AdaMEM (2606.05684) adds on-the-fly strategy memory mid-episode but never isolates timing from content and does not test harm. MemCon (2607.13591) learns a tabular UCB bandit over Retrieve/PlanInject/Re-Retrieve/NoOp and reports up to 15.2 points with no tuned static-heuristic control, no variance, no transfer. RSCB-MC (2604.27283) is a risk-sensitive contextual bandit for coding agents that picks a memory-use mode per query (no memory, top resolution, summarize candidates, high-precision or high-recall retrieval, abstain, ask for feedback); it decides what mode, not when in the episode, and its static-control and transfer story is unknown from the abstract. The proactive memory agent (2607.08716) has a second agent decide inject-or-stay-silent against within-task behavioral state decay, not cross-episode experience, and does not cost the extra agent. The Compliance Trap (2607.10608) already varies schedule (step-1-only, persistent, withheld-until-step-3) and shows harm begins at entry, but with planted task-wrong memory, a fixed step index rather than an agent-state trigger, and no mitigation. Uncertainty-triggered dynamic RAG (2501.09292, SUGAR 2501.04899) and self-triggered retrieval control at decode time (GRIP, 2604.11407) decide when to retrieve for text generation and have not been ported to experience memory on tool-use traces. Agentic-memory-as-RL-tools (2601.01885) learns retrieval actions with no transfer test; TraceRetain (2606.29178) is retention-side eviction, not timing. The survey 2603.07670 frames when-to-retrieve as an open control-policy question without data.
Abstract: Experience memories for LLM agents almost always inject retrieved items at episode start, and the recent alternative is a learned policy that decides when or whether to retrieve. Neither literature asks whether the time of injection alone changes the sign of memory's effect for the same items, and no learned policy has been compared with a tuned static trigger. We fix the bank, the query, k and the retrieved items, and vary only the reveal time: episode start, first detected stall, fixed late step, every step, reimplemented MemCon-style and RSCB-MC-style learned policies, and an oracle-timed upper bound, on ALFWorld and WebShop with three local backbones. Paired McNemar tests on identical task-seed pairs separate timing from content; a stall-triggered generic-reflection control and a stall-triggered random-item control separate memory content from a replanning nudge. Entry-Propagation-Recovery tallies against ALFWorld's expert plans test the mechanism: compliance rates should be similar across arms, but success conditional on compliance should be much higher at a stall than at entry. We then sweep the static trigger's two parameters on one backbone, freeze it, and swap backbones and environments, comparing against the learned policies frozen and relearned. The deliverable is a pre-registered answer to whether when-to-retrieve is a learning problem or a two-number heuristic, and whether the pilot's start-of-episode harm is a timing artefact.
Experiments: Environment and data: ALFWorld with the local 1,465 unique tasks; a stream of about 1,000 tasks builds two banks from the same episodes (raw trajectory snippets and ReMe-style distilled items) with the 27B agent; about 400 held-out tasks times 3 sampling seeds, extended to about 2,000 paired episodes by seed for the confirmatory arms; WebShop for environment transfer. Backbones: an 8B dense, the program's 27B dense and 120B MoE, served with vLLM. Retrieval: frozen embedding retriever, k in {1,3} (the pilot's safe dose), query = task description. Arms: (A) start-only; (B) stall-triggered reveal of the same items pre-retrieved at start (isolates timing); (C) stall-triggered with a re-query on task plus last three actions and observations (timing plus query re-conditioning); (D) persistent every-step; (E) fixed late injection at step 3 (Compliance-Trap schedule, non-adversarial items); (F1) MemCon-style tabular UCB bandit reimplemented with the same state features; (F2) RSCB-MC-style risk-sensitive bandit over modes {no memory, inject top item, inject k, abstain}; (G) oracle-timed reveal chosen post hoc from counterfactual re-runs on a 200-task subset; (H) no memory; (I) stall-triggered Reflexion-style reflection with no memory content; (J) stall-triggered random bank items. Stall detector: n consecutive steps with no inventory or location change or an invalid-action message, cap M injections per episode; n in {1,2,3}, M in {1,2,unbounded} swept on a tuning split disjoint from eval. Transfer: tune (n,M) on 27B/ALFWorld, freeze, apply to 8B, 120B and WebShop; compare with F1 and F2 frozen versus relearned on each swap with a tuning budget equal to the trigger sweep. Mechanism: per injection, record whether the next action matches an item's recommended action (compliance) and whether it is on the expert path; E-P-R tallies per arm. Cost: injected tokens per episode, extra LLM calls, wall-clock. Confirmatory set: all arms on 27B; A, B, F1, F2, H, I on 8B and 120B; A, B, F1, H on WebShop.

P5: Persistent injection (D) is not better than B and consumes at least three times the injected tokens. P6: The late fixed-step schedule (E) is worse than B, showing the trigger must be state-conditioned rather than merely delayed.

Name: wrong_action_fraction_dose
Title: Not How Many, But How Many Are Wrong: The Dose-Response of Injected Experience on Agent Traces Follows the Wrong-Action Fraction, Not Token Load or Item Count
Short Hypothesis: On tool-use traces, success as a function of injected experience is not a smooth decreasing function of injected tokens or item count; it is a step function of the number of injected items whose recommended action is off the expert path for the current task, with most of the harm arriving at the first wrong item (the 'first drop of ink' nonlinearity shown on static multi-document QA replicates on agent traces), while length-matched neutral padding to the same token count produces no measurable harm. The pilot's 7-to-3 cut worked by removing low-rank wrong-action items, not by removing tokens. Consequently a static k chosen at the knee, combined with wrong-item removal, matches a learned budget, and the knee location is invariant across backbones and across raw versus distilled items, whereas prompt position only scales the magnitude.
Related Work: The First Drop of Ink (arXiv:2605.10828) shows that the first ten percent of hard distractors causes most of the degradation in 128K multi-document QA on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-Next-80B, but studies retrieved documents, not experiential items, and never touches agent traces or the injection-budget decision. Length-alone degradation (2510.05381) and Distractor-Aware Truncation (2608.03297) separate length from signal loss on static long-context benchmarks only. The survey 2603.07670 asserts attentional dilution without data. Self-Generated In-Context Examples for sequential decision-making (2505.00234) selects self-generated trajectories as exemplars on ALFWorld and WebShop and is the nearest k-selection neighbour, but it optimizes which exemplars to keep and does not decompose dose into tokens, count and wrong-action fraction or use length-matched controls. Structured Experience Compression reports +7.7 on ALFWorld at 37 percent of raw-trajectory tokens, a granularity result with no dose sweep; Useful Memories Become Faulty (2605.12978) favours raw episodes over consolidated ones, again without a dose curve. The Trap of Trajectory (2605.09330) identifies spurious correlations in agentic memory and calibrates reliance at write and retrieval time (CAMEL), but does not sweep the number or fraction of misleading items. DeepControl (2602.01672) learns retrieval extent for search-augmented QA, not experience memory. MemCon (2607.13591) learns how much to retrieve with no static-k control. Compiled Memory (2603.15666) argues for compiling rather than injecting more, without a dose curve. The program's archived idea memory_budget_confound asserts that token volume explains both harm and gain; this proposal is its direct competitor and the experiment is designed so that exactly one of the two survives.
Abstract: Agent memory systems choose how many items to inject with no measured dose-response on agent traces; the only characterizations of injected-context harm come from static text, where length alone, attentional dilution, and a sharply nonlinear hard-distractor effect have all been reported. We characterize the dose-response of injected experience on ALFWorld and WebShop traces with three local backbones and decompose the dose into three candidate variables: token count, item count, and the number of injected items whose recommended action is off the expert path for the current task. The decomposition uses controls that static-text studies cannot: length-matched neutral padding, rank-swap reconstruction of the pilot's 7-versus-3 harm, a fixed-token budget filled at two item granularities, and a hard-distractor sweep that adds j relevance-matched wrong-action items to three correct ones. Each item's wrong-action label is computed automatically from ALFWorld's expert plans. We fit knee versus linear dose models per condition, compare a swept static k against a MemCon-style learned budget, and run Entry-Propagation-Recovery tallies to check that harm enters at the first exposed decision through the wrong item's action. The result is a pre-registered ruling on what the injection budget is a budget of, and a static rule for setting it.
Experiments: Setup: ALFWorld with the local 1,465 tasks split into bank-building (about 1,000 tasks, both raw-trajectory and ReMe-style distilled banks from the same episodes with the 27B agent) and held-out eval (about 400 tasks times seeds); WebShop replication of the core contrasts; backbones 8B dense, 27B dense, 120B MoE. Labels: for each retrieved item and each eval task, the item's recommended first action or sub-goal sequence is matched against the task's expert plan to yield right or wrong-action, computed automatically and hand-audited on 200 items. Confirmatory core on 27B at prefix position: (1) wrong-item sweep at fixed token budget, three correct items plus j in {0,1,2,4} relevance-matched wrong-action items (same objects and receptacles, different task type), padded to a constant token count; (2) pure-length sweep, three correct items plus neutral padding matched to the token count of k in {5,7,10,15} retrieved items, two padding types (in-domain rulebook paraphrase and off-domain prose); (3) rank-swap reconstruction, k=7 top retrieved versus k=7 with ranks 4-7 replaced by matched padding versus k=3 with one item replaced by a rank-7 wrong-action item; (4) fixed token budget of about 1,500 tokens filled by two raw items or eight distilled items to separate item count from token count; (5) easy-distractor control, three correct plus j random-task items. Exploratory: the same sweeps on 8B and 120B; position in {system prefix, immediately before the current observation, interleaved per step}; a MemCon-style bandit over k in {0,1,3,5,7} versus the swept static k with and without oracle wrong-item removal. Mechanism: E-P-R tallies against expert plans, recording whether the entry action equals a wrong item's recommended action. Model fitting: piecewise-linear knee versus linear versus log dose models per condition, compared by paired-bootstrap AIC with task random effects.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: no memory; standard top-k injection at each k (the ReMe/ExpeL read); exemplar selection in the style of 2505.00234 at matched k; oracle-filtered injection at k=15 (all wrong-action items removed) as the ceiling any read-time filter could reach; the learned-budget bandit. Ablations: neutral padding type (in-domain versus off-domain); relevance-matched versus random-task wrong items (hard versus easy distractors); raw versus distilled granularity at fixed tokens; three prompt positions; three backbones; k=3 versus k=1 correct base; temperature-0 replication of the core sweeps.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: Pure-length padding to the k=15 token count leaves the paired net effect within the null-replicate band; if padding alone reproduces at least half of the top-15 harm, the token-load hypothesis wins and this proposal is dead. P2: Adding one wrong-action item to three correct ones produces at least 60 percent of the harm of adding four; if the harm grows linearly in j the first-drop claim dies. P3: k=7 with ranks 4-7 neutralized is indistinguishable from k=3, and k=3 with one rank-7 wrong item reproduces at least half of the k=7 harm. P4: Relevance-matched wrong items harm more than random-task items at matched tokens by at least the MDE. P5: The knee sits at j=1 on all three backbones and for both granularities; the swept static k with wrong-item removal is within the MDE of the learned budget. P6: Position changes the magnitude by less than the difference between fillings at any position; if position effects exceed filling effects, position becomes the primary dose variable and the title is wrong. P7: E-P-R tallies show the entry action equals a wrong item's recommended action in the majority of broken episodes.
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells are paired by task and seed against the no-memory arm and against each other; McNemar exact tests on discordant pairs with fixed and broken counts reported. Null replicates for each backbone (two no-memory runs, two top-3 runs) set the discordance floor; effects below the floor or the MDE are reported as null. About 2,000 paired episodes per confirmatory cell give an MDE near 3 points. The dose curve is fit by mixed logistic regression with task random effects, condition fixed effects and cluster-robust standard errors; the knee-versus-linear comparison is pre-registered as the primary model test. Retriever and bank frozen; the wrong-action label is rule-based from expert plans, not an LLM judge, with a 200-item hand audit reported. Padding neutrality is itself tested (padding-only versus no memory). Pre-registration fixes the sweep grid, the padding types, the MDE, and the criterion for declaring the knee before the first confirmatory run.

Name: retrieved_set_disagreement_gate
Title: Abstain When They Disagree: Harm from Organically Accumulated Agent Memory Lives in the Retrieved Set, Not the Item, and a Disagreement Gate Beats Item-Level Utility Filtering at Zero Clean-Setting Cost
Short Hypothesis: When a bank is accumulated organically over a task stream with no planted conflicts, the items that break tasks are not individually low-utility; harm concentrates in retrievals where the top-k items disagree about the next action for the current state. A read-time gate that abstains from injection when a cheap action-consistency score over the retrieved set falls below a threshold, with no extra LLM call, removes at least 70 percent of the natural paired harm while keeping at least 80 percent of the gain on agreeing retrievals, whereas item-level utility filtering, validity or provenance and recency gating, spurious-cue calibration, learned abstention and reliance steering do not, because they act on item properties that do not predict which retrievals break tasks.
Related Work: The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows that consuming conflicting memory fails at entry and that stronger agents lose more once they comply, but it plants conflicts and tests no control. MemRL (2601.03192) filters by learned per-item utility; provenance gating (2608.10509) reranks by path trust on a synthetic multi-agent benchmark; reliance steering (2601.05107) makes reliance a user-set dial in conversation; TEPA (2608.07429) makes validity an explicit revocable state of memory as a lifecycle operation; PRECEPT (2603.09641) invalidates rules by Bayesian source reliability; RaMem (2606.22844) verifies relevance of retrieved fragments before synthesis; RSCB-MC (2604.27283) learns a risk-sensitive abstain decision for coding agents; CAMEL (2605.09330) calibrates reliance on spurious patterns at write and retrieval time and reports clean-input preservation. None has been shown to limit damage in task execution from naturally retrieved conflicts against each other on the same seeds, which is gap G34 verbatim, and all act on item- or feature-level properties. StateFuse (2607.05844) preserves conflicting observations in multi-agent memory and finds that preserved ambiguity enables safer abstention, but as a memory-layer design, not a retrieval-set gate on experience memory. STALE (2605.06527), MemConflict (2605.20926) and abstention under irreducible personal-memory conflict (2608.13921) are conversational or QA probes. Honest Lying (2605.29463) shows confabulated reflections persist across resets, a natural source of the wrong items studied here. Contradiction pruning in the program's pilot neutralized harm at write time but discarded the gain. The archived idea memory_item_value_reliability argues per-item utility estimates do not generalize; this proposal names the unit that does and builds the control.
Abstract: Every proposed defence against harmful retrieved memory acts on items: utility scores, validity or provenance states, recency, spurious-cue calibration, a learned abstain decision, or a global reliance setting. We test the alternative that harm from an organically accumulated experience bank is a property of the retrieved set. Over three randomized ALFWorld task streams, a 27B agent accumulates raw and distilled items through a ReMe-style write path with no planted conflicts, and banks are frozen at three checkpoints so staleness arises naturally. On held-out tasks every retrieval is labelled post hoc from expert plans and bank timestamps at the item level (right, wrong, stale, conflicting) and at the set level (agree-right, agree-wrong, disagree), and per-retrieval harm is estimated with paired no-memory runs and Entry-Propagation-Recovery tallies. A likelihood-ratio test asks which label explains broken outcomes. Eight read-time controls are then run head to head on the same seeds and banks: a disagreement gate based on a cheap action-consistency score, MemRL-style utility filtering, validity and provenance or recency gating, CAMEL-style calibration, an RSCB-MC-style learned abstain policy, reliance-steering instructions, an LLM-judge conflict verifier, and an oracle gate, each scored on harm removed, gain retained, clean-setting cost on agree-right retrievals, and token cost. A by-product is the first task-execution partition of failures into wrong retrieval, arbitration failure, and failure to apply a correctly retrieved item.
Experiments: Bank formation: ALFWorld train tasks in three randomized orders; the 27B agent runs ReMe-style writes (LLM-judge validation, retrieve-once at start, k=3) and the bank is frozen after 200, 500 and 1,000 tasks, giving nine banks; both raw and distilled item types are kept. Evaluation: about 400 held-out tasks times 3 seeds per bank checkpoint for the confirmatory arms; retrieval by a frozen embedding retriever at k=3, with a pre-registered fallback at k=5 if natural harm at k=3 is below the MDE. Labels: per item, the recommended first action or sub-goal sequence is matched against the eval task's expert plan (right or wrong), timestamps and later contradicting writes mark stale, and pairwise contradiction marks conflicting; per set, agree-right, agree-wrong, disagree, or mixed by an action-template consistency score (normalized edit distance over action templates for raw items, extracted action sequences for distilled items). Harm estimation: paired against no-memory per task-seed, E-P-R tallies per retrieval, then a mixed logistic regression of broken outcomes on item-level and set-level labels with a likelihood-ratio test. Controls, same seeds and banks: (a) ungated injection; (b) disagreement gate with threshold tau swept on a tuning split; (c) MemRL-style running-utility filter; (d) validity and provenance or recency gate (TEPA-style revocation of items contradicted by later writes plus recency preference); (e) CAMEL-style calibration reimplemented as a retrieval-time down-weighting of items whose match rests on surface cues; (f) RSCB-MC-style learned abstain policy trained on the tuning split; (g) low-reliance instruction; (h) LLM-judge conflict verifier (one extra call); (i) no memory and inject-always references; (j) oracle gate that injects only agree-right sets. Each control is scored on broken count removed, fixed count retained, success on the agree-right subset (clean-setting cost), extra tokens and calls. Backbones: 27B primary; 8B and 120B for (a), (b), (c), (f), (i). Transfer: WebShop with the gate defined over search-and-click action templates. Failure partition: wrong retrieval (no right item in set), arbitration failure (disagree set, agent adopts a wrong item), application failure (agree-right set, agent fails or does not comply).
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: ungated injection (the standard read), no memory, the oracle set gate as ceiling, and the six published control families reimplemented (utility filtering, validity and provenance or recency gating, spurious-cue calibration, learned abstention, reliance steering, LLM-judge verification), each with a tuning budget equal to the gate's tau sweep. Ablations: tau sweep; consistency score variants (first-action agreement only versus full sub-goal sequence); raw versus distilled items; bank checkpoint (200, 500, 1,000) as a staleness dose; k=3 versus k=5; the agree-wrong cell reported separately to test the competing majority-action-prior account; backbone swap for the gate; gate applied with re-retrieval (drop the disagreeing set and re-query) versus pure abstention.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1: The set-level label explains broken outcomes better than item-level labels (likelihood-ratio p<0.01) with an odds ratio of at least 2 for disagree versus agree-right; if item-level utility, validity or provenance predicts harm as well, the set-property claim is dead. P2: The disagreement gate removes at least 70 percent of the paired broken count at no more than 20 percent loss of the fixed count; utility filtering removes under 40 percent because harmful items are not low-utility on average. P3: On agree-right retrievals the gate's success is within the null band of ungated injection, whereas utility filtering and the learned abstain policy lose at least 2 points there. P4: The cheap consistency score is within the MDE of the LLM-judge verifier at zero extra calls; if the judge wins by more than the MDE the no-extra-call claim falls while the set-level claim stands. P5: If harm concentrates in the agree-wrong cell rather than the disagree cell, the gate fails and the majority-action-prior account is reported as the winner. P6: The gate's harm removal holds at all three bank checkpoints and on 8B and 120B; if it vanishes on the 120B the claim is restricted to weaker backbones. P7: CAMEL-style calibration and the learned abstain policy each remove less harm than the gate by at least the MDE, or the set-level gate is not the best control and the paper's contribution reduces to the diagnostic partition.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design by task, seed and bank checkpoint against no-memory and between controls; McNemar exact tests on discordant pairs with fixed and broken counts reported per control. Null replicates (two ungated runs per bank) set the discordance floor; effects below the floor or the MDE are reported as null. About 2,000 paired episodes per confirmatory arm give an MDE near 3 points; the three stream orders are the replication unit for organic bank formation and are reported separately before pooling. Labels are rule-based from expert plans and timestamps, hand-audited on 300 retrievals with agreement reported. The threshold tau and all control hyperparameters are set on a tuning split disjoint from eval tasks. Mixed logistic regression with task random effects and cluster-robust errors for the label comparison. Pre-registration fixes k and the fallback, the label rules, tau selection, the harm-removal and clean-cost criteria, and the competing agree-wrong prediction before the first confirmatory run.

Name: closer_beats_stronger
Title: Closer Beats Stronger: Consumer-Side Policy Proximity, Not Builder Capability, Predicts Whether Shared Agent Experience Transfers Across Backbones
Short Hypothesis: For a fixed retrieved set of experience items built by one backbone, the paired gain a consumer backbone obtains is predicted by the consumer's teacher-forced per-action log-likelihood of the builder's stored action sequences (policy proximity), and this predictor dominates builder solo success, parameter ratio and family identity; consequently there exist consumer cells in which a weaker-but-closer builder's bank beats a stronger-but-distant one, and a content-preserving re-narration of the builder's items into the consumer's own wording (actions held fixed) recovers a measurable share of the gap, which a capability ordering cannot explain.
Related Work: Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169) transfers a large teacher's hierarchical memory to small students and states that effectiveness depends on 'teacher capability and student compatibility' but never defines or measures compatibility and tests only strong-to-weak. SkillX (2604.04804) plugs a strong builder's skill base into weaker agents with no compatibility analysis. SKILL-KD (2607.28048) patches skills from teacher-student trajectory discrepancies: a builder-side fix in one direction. Model-Aware Skill Alignment (2605.30723) shows the same skill text performs differently across backbones and trains a rewriter; it treats mismatch as something to repair, not something to predict, and reports no strength-versus-proximity dissociation. Managing Procedural Memory (2606.23127) finds some skills transfer across models and others do not, without a consumer-side predictor of which. SkVM (2604.03088) analyzes capability requirements of code skills for portability, not experience memory. Demystifying Agent Skills (2608.14036) argues skills work as procedural anchors, which is consistent with a likelihood-based mechanism but is not tested across backbones. LatentMAS (2511.20639) requires identical architectures; the RL context manager (2605.30785) transfers poorly to dissimilar agents but the dissimilarity is uncharacterized. Entry-propagation-recovery (2607.10608) shows harm begins at the first exposed decision; we use its trace analysis to localize where low-proximity items derail a consumer. None of these fixes the retrieved set across consumers, measures a full builder-by-consumer grid, or tests a cheap pre-deployment predictor with a content-fixed causal intervention.
Abstract: Shared experience banks and skill libraries are increasingly built by one agent and consumed by another, yet every published transfer runs strong-to-weak on one axis and reports no rule for when it works. We propose that compatibility is a property of the consumer's policy, not of the builder's capability: an item helps when the consumer could plausibly have produced its action sequence, and hurts when it cannot execute the intermediate steps and diverges mid-plan. We build experience banks (raw successful trajectories and fixed-extractor insights) from eight local open-weight builders spanning two size axes and four families, fix the retrieved items per task so selection is identical for every consumer, and evaluate every builder-consumer cell on ALFWorld and a WebShop subgrid at a matched injection budget. For each cell we compute an offline predictor, policy proximity: the consumer's teacher-forced mean per-action log-likelihood of the retrieved builder trajectories under the consumer's own deployment prompt. We test three claims: proximity predicts paired cell gains out-of-builder better than builder solo success, size ratio or family; pre-registered reversal pairs exist where a weaker, closer builder beats a stronger, distant one; and consumer re-narration of the same items with actions held fixed, which raises proximity without changing content, recovers part of the distant-builder gap. Harm cells are localized with entry-propagation traces. All comparisons are paired on identical tasks with McNemar tests, null replicates set the noise band, and every cell is reported rather than the best. The result is a rule a practitioner can compute with one forward pass before deploying someone else's memory, and a mechanism that explains when strong-to-weak distillation is the wrong default.
Experiments: Backbones (all local, vLLM on 4xA100): Qwen3-4B/8B/14B/32B (within-family size axis), Gemma-3-12B/27B, Llama-3.1-8B/Llama-3.3-70B, gpt-oss-20B/120B (MoE); 8 of these serve as both builders and consumers in the exploratory grid, the two largest as consumers only in confirmatory cells. Build phase: each builder runs a build split (ALFWorld: roughly 1,000 of the 1,465 unique tasks; WebShop: 500 tasks) and stores successful trajectories; insights are extracted by one fixed local extractor (Qwen3-32B, ExpeL-style) so extraction quality is not a builder confound. Eval: 300 held-out ALFWorld tasks stratified over six task types, 300 WebShop tasks. Retrieval is fixed per (builder, task): top-k by task type plus bge-m3 similarity, consumer-independent, k in {1,3}, injected under a matched budget of at most 1,200 tokens. Predictors per cell: builder solo success on the build split; log parameter ratio; same-family indicator; policy proximity (mean per-action log-prob of retrieved builder action sequences under the consumer, teacher-forced on stored observations, and a version normalized by the consumer's own-trajectory log-likelihood); an executability probe on a 100-task subset (consumer given the builder trajectory as an explicit step plan). Outcome: paired gain per cell against the same consumer with no memory and against its self-built bank. Stage 1 exploratory grid: 8x8 cells x 150 tasks x two formats. Stage 2 confirmatory: 8 pre-registered cells including at least four reversal pairs, 600 paired tasks, three sampling seeds, plus the re-narration arm (consumer paraphrases retrieved items; action sequences verified identical by exact match; a content-changing rewriter in the style of 2605.30723 as an upper reference). Analysis: task-level mixed-effects logistic regression with cell random effects; leave-one-builder-out cross-validated R-squared of cell gains per predictor; McNemar for reversal pairs with Holm correction; entry-propagation traces record the first deviation step from the retrieved plan and recovery rate per cell.
Baselines and Ablations: No memory; self-built bank at the same k (consumer equals builder); length-matched decoy items (builder trajectories from a different task type) to separate load from content; raw trajectories versus fixed-extractor insights (prediction: proximity matters less for insights, which are less wording-bound); fixed retrieval versus consumer-specific retrieval to show the fixed-selection design is not what drives the result; proximity computed on non-retrieved random builder trajectories to test whether it is a global model-similarity statistic or item-specific; k = 1 versus 3; with and without one fixed hand-written instruction shared by all arms (no prompt optimization, so the instruction-versus-memory substitution question is deliberately excluded); greedy decoding versus temperature 0.6 with three seeds.
Falsifiable Predictions: (1) Leave-one-builder-out R-squared of policy proximity for paired cell gains exceeds that of builder solo success by at least 0.15 on ALFWorld and the sign of the difference replicates on the WebShop subgrid; if builder strength predicts as well or better, the central claim fails. (2) At least 2 of 8 pre-registered reversal pairs show the weaker-closer builder beating the stronger-distant builder for the same consumer with Holm-corrected McNemar p < 0.05; zero such pairs falsifies the reversal claim. (3) Content-preserving re-narration recovers at least 40 percent of the paired gap between the distant and close builder in low-proximity cells; recovery below 15 percent means proximity is a correlate, not a cause. (4) At least 70 percent of harm cells (negative paired gain beyond the noise band) fall in the lowest proximity tercile rather than the lowest builder-strength tercile, and their first-deviation step is earlier than in gain cells. (5) The proximity-by-format interaction is negative: proximity's predictive advantage shrinks for distilled insights relative to raw trajectories.
Measurement and Noise Control: Every comparison is paired on identical task instances; McNemar exact tests for cell contrasts; mixed-effects logistic model at the task level for the grid; thresholds, reversal pairs and cell list pre-registered before Stage 2. Noise band: the self-bank condition is re-scored twice with different sampling seeds in every consumer to reproduce the pilot's 0.05-0.14 replicate movement; any cell effect inside that band is reported as null. Minimum detectable effect at 600 pairs with a 0.2 discordance rate is about 5 points at 80 percent power; three seeds per confirmatory cell. Proximity is deterministic (one forward pass per retrieved item) and its dependence on the retrieved sample is bootstrapped. All 64 cells are reported, never peaks; token cost per episode and predictor compute cost are reported per arm.

Name: contributor_conflict_not_size
Title: Many Hands Spoil the Library: Cross-Contributor Conflict, Not Library Size, Degrades Shared Agent Skill Libraries, and Only Activation-Time Reconciliation Keeps Its Edge Over a Long Stream
Short Hypothesis: At matched library size, matched task-type coverage and matched injected tokens, a skill library written by several heterogeneous backbones gives a consumer lower paired success than a single-contributor library because it contains precondition-overlapping skills that prescribe different action sequences; the harm is realized only when a conflicting pair is co-retrieved, usage frequency fails to track utility because conflicting skills are exactly the ones retrieved most, and among reconciliation policies only activation-time conflict handling (abstain, or a consumer-likelihood tie-break) keeps its advantage over a 1,200-task stream with a mid-stream task-mix shift.
Related Work: SkillFlow (2604.17308) finds high skill usage does not imply utility and one model regresses below vanilla, inside a single agent's library with no contributor manipulation and no reconciliation comparison. SkillClaw (2604.08377) evolves skills collectively from many users' interactions by aggregation and does not measure conflict harm. SkillMAS (2605.09341) couples skill evolution with MAS restructuring under utility learning in one system without varying writer heterogeneity. Auditable compilation into a skill graph (2512.23760) promotes skills after verifier replay but is not compared with simpler policies. Agent Skills Can Be Harmful (2608.11888) attributes failures to a single skill by differential runs, not to interactions between skills from different writers. Useful Memories Become Faulty (2605.12978) traces regressions to the consolidation step in a single agent's memory. StateFuse (2607.05844) preserves conflicts as explicit objects in a replicated store but reports no task utility. Beyond Memory Majority (2608.19701) shows correlated multi-agent memories form false majorities in evidence arbitration for QA, not procedural conflict in task execution. Governed Shared Memory (2606.24535) names 'contradiction persistence' as a failure mode without measuring it. Entry-propagation-recovery (2607.10608) injects conflicts by hand; the stability-plasticity framing (2604.27003) is old-versus-new competition, whereas ours is writer-versus-writer competition at the same time. None manipulates contributor heterogeneity at matched size and coverage, ties harm to co-retrieval, or runs reconciliation policies head to head over a stream with a shift.
Abstract: Shared skill libraries are pitched as the multiplier of agent experience: many agents write, everyone reads. We ask what a consumer actually pays for the 'many writers' part. Holding library size, task-type coverage and injected tokens fixed, we build ALFWorld and WebShop skill libraries from one contributor, from four seeds of the same contributor, and from four heterogeneous open-weight backbones, all extracted by one fixed local extractor into a precondition/action-macro/postcondition schema with contributor tags. We define a conflict as two skills co-retrieved for the same query whose action macros diverge, detected deterministically by action-sequence alignment, and we test whether the heterogeneous library's deficit is explained by conflicts rather than by size or by one weak writer: conflicts are removed at matched size, coverage is reduced with conflicts kept, and k is dropped to one so co-retrieval cannot occur. We then run the library online over a 1,200-task stream in three orders with a task-mix shift at the midpoint and compare reconciliation policies at a fixed size cap: usage-based pruning, keep-newest, verifier-replay promotion, LLM merge, random pruning, and two activation-time policies that detect a co-retrieved conflict and either abstain or inject the skill with higher consumer likelihood. Per-skill usage is compared with leave-one-skill-out counterfactual utility to test SkillFlow's usage-utility decoupling as a consequence of conflict. All arms are paired on the same tasks with the same consumer seed schedule; three stream orders are the replicates; a null replicate sets the noise band. The outcome is a rule for how a shared library should be governed as it grows: not by how often a skill is used, and not at write time, but at the moment two writers disagree in front of the consumer.
Experiments: Contributors: Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-12B, Llama-3.1-8B, gpt-oss-20B (heterogeneous set) and four sampling seeds of Qwen3-8B (homogeneous control). Consumers: Qwen3-14B (primary), Gemma-3-27B (replication). Skills are extracted from each contributor's successful trajectories by a fixed extractor (Qwen3-32B) into {precondition: task type plus state cues; action macro; postcondition; contributor tag}. Library conditions at matched size N = 150 and matched coverage histogram over task type x receptacle class: each single contributor; heterogeneous-mixed; homogeneous-mixed; heterogeneous-mixed with conflicts removed (precondition-cluster dedupe keeping one at random, topped up from the same contributors); heterogeneous-mixed with conflicts kept but coverage reduced. Conflict detection: two skills retrieved in the same top-k whose macros disagree at the first divergent action (exact alignment), validated on 200 sampled pairs by a local judge for label sanity. Static evaluation: 600 paired tasks per condition per consumer. Online stream: 1,200 ALFWorld tasks in three fixed random orders; contributors run ahead of the consumer and write on success; the consumer's library is capped at N and governed by one policy; task-type mix shifts at task 600 (pick/clean/heat dominant to cool/examine/pick-two dominant) so earlier precondition cues go stale; success is measured in windows of 200. Policies: usage-based pruning, keep-newest, verifier-replay promotion (admit only if the consumer replays the source task successfully), LLM merge of conflicting pairs, random pruning, activation-time abstain, activation-time consumer-likelihood tie-break. Metrics: windowed paired success versus no-library; conflict incidence per retrieval; activation-conditional harm (success on retrievals containing a conflicting pair versus matched retrievals without); per-skill Spearman correlation between usage and leave-one-skill-out counterfactual utility on a 300-task subsample; tokens per episode and extractor/verifier calls per policy. WebShop repeats the static comparison and the k ablation with 300 tasks.
Baselines and Ablations: No library; raw-trajectory retrieval from the same contributors at matched tokens (the SkillEvolBench finding that raw can beat distilled); one fixed hand-written instruction present in all arms; k = 1 versus k = 3 (at k = 1 no co-retrieval exists, so conflict harm must vanish if the mechanism is right); library size sweep N in {50, 150, 400} at fixed heterogeneity to show size is not the driver; extractor ablation (contributor-self extraction versus fixed extractor); each-single-contributor baselines to rule out a single weak writer explaining the mixed deficit; length-matched decoy skills from other task types.
Falsifiable Predictions: (1) At matched N and coverage, heterogeneous-mixed minus best-single paired gain is below the negative noise band with McNemar p < 0.05 in at least 2 of 3 stream orders, while homogeneous-mixed minus single is inside the band; if heterogeneous-mixed matches or beats single (coverage diversity wins), the central claim fails. (2) Conflict removal at matched N recovers at least 70 percent of that gap, and coverage reduction with conflicts kept recovers less than 20 percent. (3) At k = 1 the heterogeneous penalty shrinks by at least 60 percent; if it persists at k = 1 the mechanism is wrong-skill content, not co-retrieval conflict, and the paper must say so. (4) Usage-based pruning does not beat random pruning at matched N (difference inside the noise band) and per-skill usage-utility Spearman rho is below 0.2. (5) The policy-by-window interaction is positive for the activation-time policies against keep-newest and verifier-replay and remains positive after the shift; if verifier-replay promotion matches the activation-time policies in the post-shift windows, the 'only activation-time survives' clause is falsified.
Measurement and Noise Control: Every arm is evaluated on identical task instances with an identical consumer seed schedule; McNemar exact tests for static contrasts; window-level mixed logistic regression with stream order as a random effect for the online comparison; three stream orders are the replicates. Null replicate: the best-single library re-run with a second consumer seed defines the noise band, and any effect inside it is reported as null. Minimum detectable effect at 1,200 paired tasks with a 0.2 discordance rate is about 3.5 points at 80 percent power; static contrasts at 600 pairs about 5 points. Conflict labels are deterministic; the pre-registered gate requires conflict incidence of at least 10 percent of retrievals in the heterogeneous library, otherwise the environment is declared unable to test the mechanism and WebShop becomes primary. Cost per episode and per policy (verifier replays, merge calls) is reported so the head-to-head is cost-matched.

Closest-method query (s2cli --recent): 'SkillFlow skill discovery repair library maintenance benchmark LLM agents skill usage utility' returned SkillFlow 2604.17308, Skill-Use 2608.04828, Dynamic Agent Skills survey 2607.10113, SkillLearnBench 2604.20087, How Well Do Agentic Skills Work in the Wild 2604.04323, SkillRevise, SkillGenBench, Agent Skills Can Be Harmful. A cross-axis S2 bulk query on provenance and shared memory also surfaced StateFuse 2607.05844, Beyond Memory Majority 2608.19701 and Governed Shared Memory 2606.24535. Assessment: no returned paper manipulates writer heterogeneity at matched size and coverage, ties harm to co-retrieved conflicting skills in task execution, or compares reconciliation policies over a stream with a shift; SkillClaw and SkillMAS are the nearest multi-writer systems and neither measures conflict harm; StateFuse preserves conflicts as a storage contract without utility measurement.
Risk Factors and Limitations: ALFWorld's small action space may yield few real conflicts once coverage is matched; the pre-registered incidence gate and WebShop's free-text actions are the mitigation. The heterogeneous deficit could stem from one poor writer rather than conflict; the each-single baselines and conflict removal at matched N separate these. A fixed extractor may homogenize skills and understate conflict, so the self-extraction ablation is reported. Online library growth is path-dependent; three orders are the replicates and the static comparison anchors the mechanism claim. The activation-time policies require a retriever that returns candidate sets, which most deployed libraries already do; the likelihood tie-break requires logprobs and therefore open-weight consumers. Results are for procedural skills; whether the same holds for factual or insight memory is not claimed.
Addresses gap: G37: how a growing shared skill library should be pruned or reconciled so that stale, conflicting or wrongly activated skills do not degrade performance over long deployment; secondary G39 (matched-cost baselines including raw-trajectory retrieval and a fixed instruction, seed variance reported).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'Write-path repairs neutralized the harm but did not convert it to gain' describes contradiction pruning on a single agent's self-built bank; this idea claims that conflicts between different writers are the harm channel in shared libraries, that they act only when co-retrieved, and that write-time repairs lose to activation-time handling over a stream. Nearest appendix ideas: memory_item_value_reliability treats utility as a per-item property, whereas this idea claims the harm is a pairwise co-retrieval property that no per-item score can capture; collection_policy_coupling_collapse studies diversity collapse from a collection policy, whereas this studies the opposite problem, excess diversity across contributors. Nearest digest card, arXiv:2604.17308 (SkillFlow): observes usage not implying utility within one agent's library; this idea explains that decoupling as a consequence of cross-contributor conflict and tests it by manipulation at matched size and coverage.

Name: lineage_blast_radius
Title: The Lineage Blast Radius: Consolidation Launders Low-Trust Experience into Shared Agent Memory, and Provenance Enforcement Pays for It in Fan-In
Short Hypothesis: In a shared experience memory that consolidates raw episodes from several contributors into insights and skills, poisoned records from one low-trust contributor survive consolidation at a rate exceeding their record share (laundering, not dilution), so record-level provenance gating that blocks them on raw records fails on derived ones; enforcing trust through lineage restores robustness but discards a fraction of the library that grows with consolidation fan-in as 1 - (1 - s)^f (s the low-trust share, f the number of sources per derived record), and trust-partitioned consolidation dominates min-trust lineage exclusion on the risk-utility frontier unless cross-trust merges carry most of the value of sharing.
Related Work: MAP-Graph (2608.10509) records provenance in a typed execution graph and propagates restrictions through derivations, evaluated on a controlled synthetic benchmark without a utility cost or a fan-in analysis. MemLineage (2605.14421) attaches cryptographic provenance and LLM-mediated derivation lineage to entries and evaluates three defense cells on a deterministic mechanism-isolation harness, not on agent task benchmarks. Manufactured Confidence (2606.29279) shows consolidation turns hedged remarks into confident facts in constructed conversational settings; it is an epistemic-laundering result on facts, not on shared experience memory, and reports no governance cost. SkillJack (2608.03509) turns poisoned histories into persistent skills that survive source deletion and motivates provenance-aware lifecycles without measuring what such lifecycles cost. OEP (2605.18930) poisons self-evolving agents with locally correct but non-transferable experiences under black-box access; defenses tested are LLM auditing only. Utility Under Attack (2608.21230) measures the utility cost of content screening and provenance ranking at retrieval and argues for bounded occupancy, with no consolidation step. Useful Memories Become Faulty (2605.12978) shows consolidation degrades memory even without an attacker, which our clean-stream control quantifies as the baseline. Collaborative Memory (2505.18279), Governed Shared Memory (2606.24535) and the Q4 write-gate audit in this brief operate at the raw-record admission level; none measures laundering versus dilution with real consolidators on agent tasks, the fan-in law for lineage cost, or partitioned versus min-trust enforcement head to head.
Abstract: Provenance is the standard answer to poisoned shared memory: tag every record with its source and exclude what is not trusted. That answer is complete only while records stay raw. Shared experience memories consolidate: episodes from many contributors are merged into insights and skills, and a derived record has many parents. We measure what happens to a low-trust contributor's content across that transformation on ALFWorld and WebShop with three honest open-weight contributors and one contributor whose successful-looking trajectories carry planted poison of three kinds (task-wrong facts, prohibited actions, and a trigger-conditioned detour), at three shares and three consolidation fan-ins, with a fixed local consolidator and exact lineage recorded. The first question is empirical and can go either way: does consolidation launder poison, amplifying it into general rules, or dilute it under the honest majority? The second is a cost law: min-trust lineage exclusion must discard every derived record with a low-trust ancestor, which we predict follows 1 - (1 - s)^f and turns into a utility loss on a clean stream once the blocked fraction is large. The third is a head-to-head on the risk-utility frontier between record-level gating, min-trust lineage, trust-partitioned consolidation, content screening, and quarantine-then-verify, including a two-round adaptive attacker who rephrases poison to survive consolidation. We also measure the cost of a wrong trust label by treating an honest contributor as low-trust. Paired task-level statistics, three consolidation seeds and a clean-stream null replicate keep the effects above the run-to-run noise that has swallowed prior claims. The outcome is a governance rule that says where in the pipeline trust must be enforced, and what a shared memory forfeits when it is.
Experiments: Environments: ALFWorld (primary, 1,465 unique tasks; targeted family for poison chosen per poison type) and WebShop (attribute poison). Contributors: Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-12B, Llama-3.1-8B (honest) plus one low-trust contributor (Llama-3.1-8B trajectories edited by a scripted attacker policy). Consumers: Qwen3-14B and Gemma-3-27B. Poison types with ground truth: (i) task-wrong facts about object locations for one task family, in OEP style locally correct on the source episode but non-transferable; (ii) a prohibited action step that violates a stated constraint in the shared instruction (measured as constraint-violation rate, in the spirit of governance decay); (iii) a SkillJack-style trigger phrase in one task family leading to a detour. Low-trust share s in {5, 15, 30} percent of raw records. Consolidation levels: L0 raw; L1 per-episode summaries (f = 1); L2 cross-episode insights with cluster size f in {3, 6, 12}; L3 skills extracted from the same clusters; consolidator Qwen3-32B (gpt-oss-120B as a second consolidator on the s = 15 percent cells); lineage recorded exactly. Governance arms: none; record-level provenance gating (low-trust raw records excluded at read time, derived records untouched); min-trust lineage exclusion (any derived record with a low-trust ancestor excluded); trust-partitioned consolidation (consolidate within trust class; low-trust class excluded before merge); content-only screening (LLM-judge validation as in ReMe and consensus checking as in A-MemGuard); quarantine-then-verify (derived records with low-trust lineage admitted only after successful consumer replay on a held-out source task). Adaptive attacker: two rounds, black-box on the consolidator, observing which of its records survived and rephrasing poison as general rules. Injection: k = 3, at most 1,200 tokens, fixed retriever. Measures: laundering fraction (share of derived records at each level carrying the planted claim, by planted lexical markers as an upper bound and a local entailment judge), attack success on 600 targeted tasks (poisoned step executed or constraint violated), paired success on 1,000 non-targeted tasks, clean-stream utility with s = 0 and with an honest contributor mislabeled low-trust, blocked fraction under lineage exclusion against 1 - (1 - s)^f, and a risk-utility frontier per arm across the (s, f) grid. Three consolidation seeds per cell.
Baselines and Ablations: No memory; raw-record memory with record-level gating (the regime in which gating is known to work); honest-but-mislabeled contributor to separate label cost from poison; consolidator ablation (two consolidators); fan-in sweep at fixed s and share sweep at fixed f; poison-type ablation; consumer ablation; length-matched decoy records; lineage granularity ablation (exact lineage versus cluster-level lineage as a cheaper approximation); k = 1 versus 3 to check that the laundering harm is not a load effect.
Falsifiable Predictions: (1) Laundering: at s = 15 percent and f = 6, the fraction of L2 and L3 derived records carrying the planted claim exceeds s by a factor of at least 1.5; if it is at or below s (dilution), the laundering premise fails and prediction 2 is expected to fail with it. (2) Under record-level gating, attack success on targeted tasks at L2/L3 exceeds L0 by at least 10 points (paired McNemar p < 0.05); if consolidation instead lowers attack success, consolidation is protective and the headline flips. (3) The blocked fraction under min-trust lineage exclusion matches 1 - (1 - s)^f within 5 points across the grid, and its clean-stream utility loss exceeds the noise band once the blocked fraction passes 40 percent; a utility loss flat in f falsifies fan-in as the cost driver. (4) Trust-partitioned consolidation retains at least 90 percent of ungoverned clean-stream utility at every f while keeping attack success within 3 points of min-trust lineage; if partitioning loses more than the noise band relative to ungoverned consolidation, cross-trust merges carry the sharing value and 'dominates' is falsified, which the paper then reports as where the value of sharing sits. (5) Adaptive rephrasing raises attack success under content-only screening by at least 10 points and leaves the lineage and partitioned arms within the noise band.
Measurement and Noise Control: All task-level comparisons paired on identical tasks with McNemar exact tests; the (s, f) grid, poison families and thresholds pre-registered; consolidation seed treated as a random effect with three seeds per cell because the consolidator is stochastic and is itself a known variance source; null replicate: clean stream, ungoverned, two consumer seeds, defines the noise band (expected 0.05-0.14 as in the pilot). Minimum detectable effect at 600 paired targeted tasks about 5 points at 80 percent power; clean utility on 1,000 non-targeted tasks gives about 4 points. Laundering fractions carry binomial confidence intervals over roughly 300 derived records per level and are reported with both the lexical-marker bound and the judge estimate. Token cost per episode, consolidation calls and verification replays are reported per arm so the frontier is cost-annotated.

Assessment: the mechanism space is crowded on the attack side (SkillJack, OEP, Manufactured Confidence) and the mechanism side (MemLineage, MAP-Graph), so the contribution is deliberately the measurement they lack: laundering versus dilution rate with real consolidators on agent task benchmarks, the fan-in cost law for lineage enforcement, the mislabeled-contributor cost, and partitioned versus min-trust on a risk-utility frontier; no returned paper reports any of these. Risk Factors and Limitations: Laundering rates may be consolidator-specific; two consolidators are run and the effect is reported per consolidator. Detecting the planted claim in derived text is imperfect; lexical markers give an upper bound and the judge a lower one, and both are reported. ALFWorld's poison targets are limited to locations and constraint violations, so WebShop's attribute poison is the second environment. Exact lineage is recorded here, which is the best case for lineage arms; the cost measured is therefore a lower bound and the cluster-level ablation shows how it grows with coarser lineage. Trust labels at write time are assumed available, as in MAP-Graph and Collaborative Memory; the mislabeled-honest arm bounds the cost of getting them wrong. The adaptive attacker is two rounds and scripted, not an optimizer; stronger adaptive attacks are out of scope. No private, clinical or user data is involved; poison is planted in synthetic trajectories over public benchmarks.
Addresses gap: G38: robustness of provenance and isolation mechanisms to laundering through transformed views, and the utility cost of governance, measured on agent task benchmarks rather than synthetic tasks; secondary G37 (wrong records in a growing shared library).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'Write-path repairs neutralized the harm but did not convert it to gain' concerns contradiction pruning on a self-built bank; this idea concerns whether trust survives multi-contributor consolidation at all and what enforcing it costs as a function of fan-in. The Q4 write-gate audit proposes precision/recall of admission gates on planted raw records; this idea starts after admission and claims the derived-record level is where gating breaks, a failure the audit cannot see. No appendix idea addresses poisoning or provenance; the nearest, provenance_gap_selection_not_authorship, is about a writer-reader capability gap and makes no claim about trust lineage. Nearest digest card, arXiv:2608.10509 (MAP-Graph): proposes derivation-propagated provenance on a synthetic benchmark; this idea measures the laundering rate with real consolidators, the 1 - (1 - s)^f cost law, the mislabeled-contributor cost, and partitioned versus min-trust enforcement on ALFWorld and WebShop.
